# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose push/open GitHub never
  # turns into a pull_request run — the recursion guard) can still get this
  # suite started on its branch: baselining's deliver() and any bot-authored
  # PR flow (#432, #565) dispatch it explicitly.
  workflow_dispatch:
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Check out the PR's real head, not the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit
          # actions/checkout uses by default — otherwise HEAD is an ephemeral merge of
          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests
        # THE test roots — a closed set of FOLDERS, each swept to any depth. Depth is
        # deliberately not enumerated: the previous form spelled out one glob per level
        # (`packs-tests/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs` and so on), so a test at an unlisted depth
        # was silently never run — which is exactly how vendoring/'s two files sat outside
        # CI. `**` removes depth from the question; what remains is the root list, and
        # engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the moment a tracked test lands
        # outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit; adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ (migrations included) + the other top-level canon code;
        #                            mirrors engine/'s inner structure, and stays canon-side
        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)
        #   packs-tests/             every canon pack's tests, mirroring packs/
        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover
        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs
        #   .claudinite/local/packs/ this repo's own local packs — tests live inside the tree
        #   docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/ the dispatch design's executable scenarios — the
        #                            simulator lives beside the spec it models, not in
        #                            engine/ (nothing ships it; it tests prose)
        # nullglob: a root with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          tests=(engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs vendoring/**/*.test.mjs dev/tools/**/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/**/*.test.mjs docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/**/*.test.mjs)
          # Deliberately oversubscribed. node --test defaults to one worker per core
          # minus one, which fits a CPU-bound suite; this one spends most of its wall
          # clock waiting — on git plumbing, spawned workers and converge fixtures — so
          # the cores idle at that default (measured on this tree: 106s wall against
          # 187s of user+sys on 4 cores). Doubling the workers: 106s -> 70s, with 16
          # buying only another 2s.
          node --test --test-concurrency=$(( $(nproc) * 2 )) "${tests[@]}"

{"number":841,"title":"pack.json migration plan: engine reader + canon conversion, then a versioned fleet migration","body":"Executes #564 (re-evaluated 2026-08-14; PR #569 reviewed for insights and closed). Owner-settled decisions this plan encodes:

- **`pack.schema.json` is authoring tooling** (editor autocomplete + documentation). Manifest conformance — field shapes, the 20-word routing cap, skills↔tree, rule-scope agreement, the accounted-for-`.mjs` guard — is **checked by the world sweep when the file is edited**, not at load. The loader stays minimal and fail-soft: parse, resolve filenames, surface unreadable/unparseable as blocking config findings (as today).
- **`detect` is data for 14 of 17 packs** (path matching + content matching, full-noun-phrase keys per the #789/#799 discipline); sibling `detect.mjs` for chrome-extension, chrome-extension-release, static-website.
- **Members' local packs convert via a `basics` migration record with `applyStage`**; the routing gap that makes `basics` the carrier for an engine-owned format is #840.

Owner approval points: **two PRs** (plus one small telemetry-gated retirement PR later). Everything else lands through the members' own auto-merged update PRs.

## PR 1 — the engine reads pack.json; the whole canon converts

One PR: the reader and the corpus it reads must land transactionally, and the home (no mount, runs repo-root code) is the first consumer either way.

- [ ] `engine/pack_loader/pack.schema.json` — the authoring spec; its field order is the one canonical order (no second list).
- [ ] Registry reads `pack.json`: prefers it where `pack.mjs` coexists (a half-finished conversion must not resolve to the old shape), reports the leftover module for deletion, stamps `manifestFile` so findings name the consumer's actual file. The `pack.mjs` import path stays as the tolerance branch.
- [ ] `detect` spec compiler (tracked-path + file-content matching), with the #569-style equivalence tests: each compiled spec proven to mean exactly what the arrow it replaces meant — including the near-root `maxDepth` semantics and the jwt/web-speech/leaflet content-regex shape.
- [ ] Sibling code files named from the JSON: `detect.mjs` ×3, `env.mjs` where env is a function of config (node; flutter's static shell as data if the spec carries a line list, else a second `env.mjs`), `contributed.mjs` ×2 (barriers, canary-probe); `contributes` becomes a map of pack id → rule filenames; `worldRules`/`workRules` become filename lists (manifest placement stays the scope authority — #555; `declared-checks.json` stays structural with no manifest line — #827).
- [ ] Manifest conformance moves to the world sweep: schema shape, routing word cap, skills↔tree, scope agreement, and the every-`.mjs`-at-pack-root-accounted-for guard. Author each check first and watch it fail (a deliberately broken fixture AND a live in-scope count over the real tree — a path-pattern check that reaches zero files passes silently).
- [ ] Convert all 33 canon manifests + the home's 2 local packs; genuinely unhoused comments move to each pack's README (#569's second commit has the survey).
- [ ] Repoint every `pack.mjs` reader, enumerated from `grep -rl 'pack\.mjs'` in-branch (today: `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs`, sheepdog `fleet-pack-seeds`, `adopt-claudinite` interview, `converge-wiring`, the seededByDefault audit, the pack-prose narration rule, ~20 test fixtures). Fixtures author `pack.json` and copy `engine/pack_loader/` wholesale rather than enumerating its modules.
- [ ] Full suite via `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`; conformance sweep green; both hand-maintained tallies recomputed (not incremented) if checks were added; suite re-run against current `main` immediately before merge.

**Verified in-session**: the home *is* the corpus, so a green selftest + world sweep on the converted tree is a real end-to-end run of the reader — plus one member repo attached read-only to confirm nothing in its (unconverted) mount breaks against canon-side tasks that read packs from a fresh clone.

## Between PRs — the release gate

- [ ] Run the live canary rehearsal against the merged snapshot; watch it to a terminal state (a dispatch is not a result). Note its known blind spot: it drives the worker *this ref ships*, so it cannot see a fielded-caller break — hence the next checkbox.
- [ ] Confirm nothing under `updates/*` (the flow surface fielded workers call) changed shape in PR 1; if anything did, shim per the live-cross-version-API discipline before releasing.

## PR 2 — the release and the fleet migration record, one change

Per `engine/migrations/README.md`, a record lands in the same change as the bump it names:

- [ ] `ENGINE_VERSION` 4 → 5 (the engine that reads pack.json).
- [ ] `basics` version 2 → 3, `minEngineVersion: 5` — the updater's own enforcement guarantees no member converts its local packs before holding the engine that reads the result.
- [ ] `packs/basics/migrations/2026-08-XX-local-pack-json/migration.mjs`:
  - `applyStage: { why, instructions }` — convert this repo's local packs to `pack.json` (+ sibling `.mjs` only where a manifest genuinely holds code), move manifest comments to the pack README, delete `pack.mjs`, repair the member's own pack tests.
  - `legacyPresent` probes every declared local pack (both local-pack roots) for a surviving `pack.mjs` — the fleet census reads it, so "is the fleet done" is telemetry, not memory.
  - `appliesTo` probes the member's own mount for the pack.json-capable registry **by content, not version stamp** — fail-safe (unreadable mount = not capable), so the record delays instead of wedging (the sheepdog-fleet-baseline lesson).

## Same-session fleet verification — not "after the nightly"

- [ ] Force the fleet baseline/update sweep with `follow`; report per-member results unasked, attaching member repos directly rather than offering to.
- [ ] Drive one member that carries local packs through its update **now**; watch the `applyStage` session convert them and the auto-merged PR land green.
- [ ] Judge freshness by each member's stamp `ref`/engine version, never `updated` alone (held stamps), and read the **status** of every API write, not just its body.
- [ ] Report the `legacyPresent` census: which members still hold a `pack.mjs`, driven by the standing update mechanism — no phase anyone must remember to close.

## Retirement — telemetry-gated, expiry-pinned

- [ ] PR 1 ships a pinned-expiry test on the both-shapes tolerance (re-check at a named engine version), so retirement has a trigger that comes to us.
- [ ] When the census reads clean **from the members' repos, not by reasoning about canon**: one small PR deletes the `pack.mjs` read branch and the legacy fixtures. The record itself stays, as history.

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it

- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left).

content.content:
## Part 5 — wire the hooks

Claude Code runs `SessionStart` entries **in parallel, in non-deterministic order**, so anything
sequenced must live inside **one** entry. Register exactly one — the orchestrator, which runs
the context steps in sequence in a single process (self-test → active-pack prose → each
active pack's own session-start step → skill mounts → env check → interview check) and forwards their stdout into the session context:

```json
{ "hooks": { "SessionStart": [ { "hooks": [
  { "type": "command", "command": "bash $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/session-start-command.sh" }
] } ] } }
```

Register the Stop hook (runs the **work-scope** checks when the session changed something —
judging the change in front of the session, with the transcript — and blocks the stop while
blocking findings remain), the PreToolUse guard (deterministically blocks forbidden commands),
and the SessionEnd runner (invokes each active pack's own `session-end.mjs`, once, when the
session ends — best-effort and fail-soft: it can never block a session from ending, and nothing
depends on it having run) alongside it. The **world-scope** sweep is not wired here — it goes
into the project's test/CI flow in Part 8:

```json
{ "hooks": { "Stop": [ { "hooks": [
  { "type": "command", "command": "node $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/stop-command.mjs" }
] } ],
  "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [
  { "type": "command", "command": "node $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/pretooluse-command.mjs" }
] } ],
  "SessionEnd": [ { "hooks": [
  { "type": "command", "command": "node $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/session-end-command.mjs" }
] } ] } }
```

Invoke scripts **through `bash`/`node`**, never as bare paths — a dropped exec bit would fail the
hook before line 1 and swallow its own message. Notes on how the steps behave:

- **A pack may contribute its own session-start step** — the orchestrator runs
  `<pack>/session-start.mjs` for every declared pack that ships one, hands it that pack's
  entry `config`, and forwards what it prints into the session context under the pack's
  marker. It is for what a pack can only know at session time (content from outside this
  repo, or keyed to the person in front of it), where `RULES.md` is fixed at vendor time.
  Bounded and **fail-soft**: a step that fails, hangs, or overruns the context cap is one
  plain-text note and the session proceeds. Which packs contribute one is the packs'
  business, not bootstrap's.
- **The session opens by stating what loaded** — a last step counts the active packs, their
  checks, the token weight of the prose injected and the skills mounted, and emits that as one
  line the session repeats back before anything else. A pack whose step computed something worth
  adding to it says so on the facet channel (a `CLAUDINITE-FACET:` line), which the orchestrator
  opens and cleans up; core learns no pack's name to carry a facet.
- **The halt-gate** — a SessionStart hook cannot block, but its stdout is injected into context,
  so a step that can't do its load-bearing job (`env.mjs check` — a missing toolchain) prints a
  plain-text directive telling the assistant to STOP and confirm via `AskUserQuestion` before any
  work. Plain text always — one hook's stdout must never mix JSON and prose.
- **The durable hook log** — every hook appends `start` / `done exit=N` lines to
  `.claudinite-hooks.log` at the repo root. No lines ⇒ the hook never triggered; `start` without
  `done` ⇒ it died executing. Reach for it first when a session says the harness didn't load.
- **Skill mounts are session-generated, never committed** — `shared/engine/skill_loader/mount-skills.mjs`
  (an orchestrator step) regenerates `.claude/skills/<name>` symlinks for the declared packs'
  union each session and maintains a self-ignoring `.gitignore` there; a committed link would
  dangle on every plain checkout.

One standing rule the vendored tree does **not** change: committed consumer code must not
`import`/`require` canon helpers from `.claudinite/` — the canon is refreshed nightly and
refactored upstream, so code reaching into it inherits every rename as a breaking change. Inline
what you need. The `claudinite-isolation` check enforces this outside the wiring files.

## Part 6 — schedule the repo (it schedules itself)

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm

## Part 6 — schedule the repo (it schedules itself)

A consuming project schedules **itself** (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §9). As part of
adoption:

1. **Vendor the scheduler workflow** — copy `claudinite-scheduler.yml` into
   `.github/workflows/` and rewrite its placeholder cron minute to this repo's stable
   hashed minute in :10–:50 (the repo's only cron). Compute the minute — never guess it —
   with the vendored hasher: `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs
   <owner/repo>`. It is a pure function of the repo full name, so it is the same value on
   every re-vendor and the update task re-derives it to catch drift. This step, the Part 5
   hook registrations, dropping the retired `@.claudinite/shared/CLAUDE.md` import, the
   rules index (`.claudinite/claudinite-rules.GENERATED.md` and its `CLAUDE.md` import), this
   repo's own seed local pack, and the README pack-badge row (below)
   are all mechanized by `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs
   <owner/repo> --badges --seed-local-pack` — the single wiring surface bootstrap and the update
   flows both call, so the set is defined once in code, not re-enacted from this prose each
   night. Pass both flags here and only here: they are the surfaces adoption seeds that the
   nightly deliberately does not (step 2).
2. **The README pack-badge row needs no step either** — the same converge writes a
   one-line row of the declared packs' badges into `README.md`, under the title, between
   `<!-- claudinite:packs -->` markers — the opening one on its own line above the badges,
   so the badges are not swallowed by the HTML block a line beginning with `<!--` opens;
   anything the repo writes after the closing marker
   on that line is its own and is never touched. **This is a one-time seed.** Baselining
   runs the same converge WITHOUT `--badges`, so from here the row is the repo's own text
   — edit it, move it, or delete it, and nothing will argue. A README belongs to its repo,
   and a nightly-derived row would put a README diff in the update commit every time
   the declaration moved.
3. **Labels need no step** — the scheduler ensures `ready-for-agent`,
   `agent-running`, `needs-human`, and `workflow-failure` exist (create-if-missing,
   idempotent) before it dispatches, so they materialize on the first run and
   self-heal if deleted. No one-off creation, nothing to forget.
4. **Write the `taskScheduler` key** into `.claudinite-checks.json` (defaults:
   `{ "dailyHour": 4, "weeklyDay": "Sun", "monthlyDay": 1 }`, all UTC) — this is the
   cutover marker: the central routine stops planning the repo the same night, and its
   own scheduler + self-update take over the refresh.
5. **Create the label-wired executor routine** via the trigger API, named
   `Claudinite executor - <repo>`, with the launcher prompt
   `Execute the Claudinite executor: .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/executor.md`.
   The finished routine fires on the `ready-for-agent` label event, runs Sonnet 5, and
   has sources = **this repo alone** (not the Claudinite canon — task-prework
   DESIGN §7/E5: the update runner fetches canon Action-side, so no executor task needs it in
   session).

   The API sets only name, prompt and environment; **the repo binding, the trigger
   event, the label filter and the model are UI-only**, so every routine an agent
   creates arrives unfinished. Do not file a separate issue for the remainder — a
   config that lives away from the thing it configures is a config someone reads once
   and never reconciles. **Carry the leftover steps in the routine's own prompt**, as a
   block below the launcher line whose last instruction is to delete itself:

   > `--- SETUP — delete this block once done, leaving only the line above ---`
   > 1. Model → Sonnet 5.
   > 2. Repo → `<owner>/<repo>`, and that repo alone (source and outcome).
   > 3. GitHub trigger → "Issue: Labeled".
   > 4. Filter → Labels: is one of: `ready-for-agent`.

   The routine then states its own unfinished-ness where the owner is already looking to
   fix it, and finishing it and clearing the block are the same edit — so a
   half-configured executor cannot quietly pass for a working one.

During the rollout the owner drives each repo's cutover in a session (MIGRATION.md); the
old enrollment issue and the central routine are retired at Phase 4.

## Part 7 — categorize the project (declare its class pack)

**Only for a fresh / empty project** — one without its own established working style. The owner
runs recurring **classes** of project, each carried by a project-class pack:

1. Ask the owner which class this project is, offering the project-class packs under
   [`packs/`](packs/) as the options.
2. A class pack fits → add its id to `"packs"` in `.claudinite-checks.json` and re-run Part 3
   (a declaration change triggers a whole-set refresh, so the new pack's content lands).
3. No class pack fits → run the project-instructions skill: it decomposes the project into pack
   facets and extracts its working instructions into new/refined canon packs (the primary
   deliverable) plus a thin project-specific overlay.

## Part 8 — wire the world sweep into the test/CI flow, and land green

The **world-scope** sweep is a whole-repo invariant assertion — the same shape as a test suite —
so it runs wherever the project runs its tests, not on the Stop hook. Wire it in as its own step,
invoked as the standalone command (it is the engine's always-vendored Node CLI, so it runs in any
flow regardless of the project's own language — **never** add it as a language-specific test file
a runner discovers):

```sh
node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
```

- **The project already has a test/CI flow** (a CI job, a `make test` target, an npm/pnpm
  `test` script, a `justfile`, …): add the command above as one more step, so a red world sweep
  fails that flow exactly like a failing test. Only the world sweep goes here — the **work** scope
  judges a session's own change and runs at that session's Stop hook, not in the test/CI flow.
- **The project has none:** add a **minimal** flow — a single CI job (or a `make`/script target)
  whose steps run the project's own tests, if any, then the world command above. The point is a
  deterministic place the whole-repo sweep runs at each change; keep it as small as the repo needs.

Then run the world sweep once locally and clear what it surfaces. On a repo with existing code,
**expect a backlog** — enforcement scope is whole-repo, and findings in code you never touched
would otherwise fail every future run. Fix causes, or record a reasoned `accept` in
`.claudinite-checks.json` for the deliberate keeps. Don't reach for `--changed` to hide the
backlog — it is a transitional aid, never the enforcement default. Commit the adoption as one
change (the vendored tree, the declaration, the hook wiring, the test/CI step) and push it
through the normal PR flow.

## Part 9 — cloud environment setup (Claude Code on the web)

The web base image ships no toolchains; installs belong in the environment **image** (built
once, snapshotted), not a per-session hook. The corpus holds the one generic script —
[`engine/hooks/environment-setup-command.sh`](engine/hooks/environment-setup-command.sh), vendored into
`.claudinite/shared/engine/vendoring/` — identical for every project: paste its full body into the
environment's **Setup script** field and rebuild. It runs each active pack's declared installs
(`env.mjs install`, driven by the declaration); the SessionStart `env.mjs check` then only
*probes* and halt-gates on a genuinely missing prerequisite. The network policy must reach what
the active packs install from (npm registry, `pub.dev`, …) — the corpus itself is already in the
checkout.

## Bespoke merge policy (optional)

The portable merge recipe ships as the merge skill and needs nothing from you (squash via PR,
gate on CI only when the repo has it). Only if your project genuinely diverges: put the policy in
its own file and **name it explicitly in your `CLAUDE.md`** — the recipe reads it only then.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.

- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.

Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.

Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.

- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. - single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it

- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If

content.content: Launching skill: single-issue-triage

1	# Baseline migrations (`engine/migrations/`) — declared path relocations, applied by each member itself
2	
3	> The **baseline migrations** mechanism, and the machinery that runs it (this README,
4	> `registry.mjs`, `apply.mjs`). Every migration ever landed lives in one folder —
5	> `<landed-date>-<slug>/migration.mjs` — **under the flow that owns it**: an engine change beside
6	> this file, a pack's own change under `packs/<pack>/migrations/`
7	> (docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md §3.7). Discovery walks both, so a caller never asks which.
8	> Records are never retired, archived, or deleted: the full history is the durable backfill
9	> source, and **fetching decides relevance** — vendoring ships a consumer only the records landed
10	> within the last 7 days, while a dormant project baselining out of a fresh canon clone sees them
11	> all and applies what it needs. The code identifiers stay `*Migrations`; "baseline migration" is
12	> what to call the mechanism.
13	
14	When the canon renames or relocates an artifact that consumers hold their own copy of — a tracked
15	file, a `settings.json` registration, a stub, a path a check or script references — the consumer's
16	copy doesn't move on its own. Historically each such rename grew its own scattered tolerance
17	(`LEGACY_STUB_NAMES` in a check, a `.gitkeep` fallback in the sync script and again in the census, a
18	Part-3b step in bootstrap) with **no single home**. A **baseline migration** closes that gap: one
19	declarative record per rename, discovered structurally (any `<flow>/migrations/<date>-<slug>/migration.mjs`,
20	like packs and skills), that supplies the read-side resolver and the write-side rename.
21	
22	## A baseline migration
23	
24	```js
25	// An illustrative record (the shape, not a live migration): the historical
26	// mount-folder relocation, which moved the tracked sync hook into mount/.
27	// Lives at engine/migrations/2026-07-13-mount-folder-relocation/migration.mjs.
28	export default {
29	  id: 'mount-folder-relocation',
30	  landed: '2026-07-13',                 // date it merged to canon (YYYY-MM-DD; = the folder prefix)
31	  version: 4,                           // the OWNING FLOW's version this change takes effect at —
32	                                        // a repo below it still needs the record, one at or above
33	                                        // it has already had it applied. Land it with that bump.
34	  summary: 'sync hook + orchestrator + env-setup bundled into a mount folder',
35	  aliases: [{ canonical: '.claudinite/mount/sync-claudinite.sh',
36	              legacy: ['.claudinite/sync-claudinite.sh', '.claude/hooks/sync-claudinite.sh'] }],
37	  legacyPresent: async (exists) => exists('.claudinite/sync-claudinite.sh'),
38	};
39	```
40	
41	## Two jobs, two consumers
42	
43	- **Read — "prefer Y, fall back to X".** [`resolvePath(migrations, canonical)`](registry.mjs) returns
44	  `[canonical, ...legacy]`. A tolerance point (a check, a script) consults this instead of hardcoding
45	  its own `LEGACY_*` constant, so the accepted shapes for a path are declared **once, here**.
46	- **Write — "and rename X → Y" (plus vendor, rewrite and declare).** [`applyFileAliases`](registry.mjs) moves
47	  each legacy file to its canonical path when the legacy exists and the canonical doesn't. Three more
48	  write ops cover changes a rename can't express:
49	  [`applyMaterializations`](registry.mjs) **vendors** a pack's templates into the repo's own tree
50	  (copies each `{ template, dest }` from the canon/mount to the consumer, overwriting on drift),
51	  [`applyRewrites`](registry.mjs) applies in-place `{ file, replace: [{ from, to }] }` edits
52	  (repointing refs while preserving the rest of the file), and
53	  [`applyPackDeclarations`](registry.mjs) **declares a pack** the member doesn't carry yet — each
54	  `{ id, config }` added to `.claudinite-checks.json`'s `packs` when absent, filling in a `config`
55	  only where the entry has none, because a pack the repo already declares (and the parameters it
56	  chose) are that repo's decisions. It is the shape a fleet-wide *capability* change has: a pack
57	  every member should run, whose parameters the canon knows and the member cannot derive
58	  (`materialize` would clobber a per-repo declaration; `rewrite` has no literal in common across
59	  repos). Declaring a pack whose code is not yet in the member's mount would be a blocking `config`
60	  error there, so baselining **re-converges the mount** whenever this pass changed the declaration.
61	  All honor an optional `appliesTo(read)` gate so a migration only touches the repos it's meant for
62	  (never the canon itself). [`apply.mjs`](apply.mjs) runs all four over a checkout
63	  (`node engine/migrations/apply.mjs`); idempotent, a no-op once done. Each member migrates **itself**:
64	  the update flows run the applier from the fresh canon clone they fetched, **after** the vendor step, so a
65	  key and the engine version that accepts it always land in the same transactional commit. There is
66	  no fleet-wide apply pass and no central delivery — the member's own maintenance commit carries its
67	  migration writes.
68	
69	## The version a record declares
70	
71	`version` is the number of the flow that owns the record — the engine's
72	(`engine/RELEASES.md`) for a record under `engine/migrations/`, that pack's for one
73	under `packs/<pack>/migrations/` — **at which its change takes effect**. So a record
74	lands in the same change as the bump it names, and the whole question "does this
75	record still apply to that repo" is `record.version > repo's installed version`
76	(`migrationApplies`, in the engine helper).
77	
78	Keep the field a **plain integer literal on its own line**. Every caller of the
79	predicate is synchronous — `migrationActive` is called from inside check bodies —
80	so the version is read out of the source rather than by importing the spec, and a
81	computed or inlined value would be invisible to that read. The two readings are
82	drift-guarded by a test that imports every real record and compares.
83	
84	## Relevance is decided at fetch time, not by a cleanup pass
85	
86	There is no retirement, no archive, and no TTL mover. All records are equal; three readers each take
87	the slice they need:
88	
89	- **Apply/backfill** ([`loadMigrations`](registry.mjs)) loads **every** record present. In a fresh
90	  canon clone that is the full history, so a dormant project that fell behind and only now baselines
91	  still catches up on everything it missed — `apply.mjs` is idempotent, so records it already
92	  applied are no-ops.
93	- **Vendoring** ([`compute-vendor-set.mjs`](../../vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs)) ships a consumer
94	  mount only the records **above the versions that repo has installed**
95	  (`migrationApplies`, [engine/checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs](../checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs)).
96	  An up-to-date repo carries none; a lagging one carries exactly its gap, however old those records
97	  are. A repo whose stamp says nothing about a flow — one that has not converged since versions
98	  existed, or a fresh adoption — falls back to the landed-date window (7 days), which is what every
99	  member had before versions: unknown is answered as unknown, never as version zero.
100	- **Check-tolerance** ([`migrationActive(slug)`](../checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs))
101	  answers true only for a record that is present **and** still applies by that same predicate — one
102	  shared function, so "shipped to the mount" and "tolerated by a check" can never mean different
103	  things. In a member the answer therefore reduces to "is the record in my mount": the gate that put
104	  it there is the gate that tolerates it.
105	
106	A tolerance that cannot be expressed through `migrationActive`/`resolvePath` — one living inline in
107	a check or script — is swept by hand when the transition is over; the record itself just stays, as
108	history.
109	
110	## Adding one
111	
112	1. Drop a `<flow>/migrations/<landed-date>-<slug>/migration.mjs` exporting the spec above (folder
113	   prefix = the `landed` date), under the flow whose change it repairs — `engine/migrations/` for an
114	   engine contract, `packs/<pack>/migrations/` for one pack's. Structural discovery picks it up —
115	   no list to edit. Declare the `version` its change takes effect at, and bump that flow's version in
116	   the same change; without a version the record falls back to the date window and stops applying
117	   after 7 days, whatever state the fleet is in.
118	2. Point every reader of the old path at `resolvePath(...)`, or gate an inline tolerance on
119	   `migrationActive('<slug>')` so it ends itself when the record ages out of the window.
120	3. There is no step 3 — the record ships to consumers for 7 days, every member applies it on its own
121	   next converge, and the folder remains here as the durable backfill for the long tail.
122

Status note from the #649 verification run; nothing here is decided or changed.

One risk this issue carries implicitly is now retired. The acceptance probe — "purge all release aspects from MissingBulbWebsite so it simulates a fresh repo, adopt the pack, and the first release works on the first go" — depends on `static-website`'s `static-site-vendoring` record materializing four workflows into the repo's own `.github/workflows/`. The pack has zero adopters, so that record had never delivered anything to anyone.

Nor had **any** record: a `materialize` whose `dest` is under `.github/workflows/` had never run against a live member, which is the residual #649 was reopened for. It is not a benign untested path — the update flow commits with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, GitHub refuses it there, and the refusal rejects the *whole ref*. A broken lane would have failed the first adopter's entire converge, and the acceptance probe would have been the thing that discovered it.

Verified end to end on the canary on 2026-08-14 (evidence on #649), through the same `write` `static-site-vendoring` uses: withheld to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, carried in the PR, parked at `apply-stage`, moved into `.github/workflows/` byte-for-byte by a session, staging swept.

So the vendoring half of the adoption path is no longer an unknown going into this work. One caveat found in the same run and worth knowing before the probe is timed: the apply stage did not merge its own PR, so delivery waited for the next cycle's disposal — on a daily `update`, up to 24h. Fix in #832; without it, "the first release works on the first go" could look like a failure that is really a wait.

The design's open questions, lifted out of `DESIGN.md` so they are decidable here rather than inside a merged doc. Nothing is decided or changed by this comment.

The design landed in #723. Three questions it deliberately left to the owner:

### 1. Pack name — `static-website` or `github-pages-serving`?

Cosmetic. The task framing called for a "github-pages-serving pack", but the pack owns versioning and the CI gate as well as the Pages deploy, so the broader name is arguably the more accurate one. **Default if unanswered: keep `static-website`** — renaming costs a vendored-path migration across adopters and buys nothing the id doesn't already say.

### 2. EdFringeNow data refreshes — `deploy-only`, or full releases?

This is the one with a live consequence, and **as adopted neither behaviour is happening**. EdFringeNow's #319 states the expectation that hourly refreshes keep cutting releases ("roughly 17/day"). They don't: the refresh task runs inside the scheduler workflow and pushes with its `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which fires no `push` event, so the release orchestrator never starts.

Confirmed against the repo since adoption:

- `bb3089c` (2026-08-12 05:22Z, "Refresh Fringe data (daily top-up)" — a scheduler-authored push into the publish set) cut **no release**. The data went live 7.5 hours later, carried incidentally by `v1.60812.1`, which was triggered by a human PR merge.
- Four releases in the five days since adoption, against five version bumps on the single day before it.
- Nothing has landed in `data/` since that release, so the live site is not stale *right now* — the gap has bitten once, visibly, rather than continuously. The daily-instead-of-hourly change (EdFringeNow #340) narrows the exposure but does not touch the cause.

So the question is not "which cadence do we prefer" but "what should a data push do", and either answer needs wiring that doesn't exist yet:

- **`deploy-only`** (the design's D5/D6 recommendation): the refresh task dispatches the release workflow in a mode that assembles and deploys the current tip without bumping, tagging, or cutting a Release. Fresh data reaches the site; tags keep naming content releases.
- **Full releases per data push**: same dispatch wiring, no new mode — accept a tag + GitHub Release per refresh (~1/day at the current cadence, ~17/day if hourly returns next festival).

Doing nothing keeps today's behaviour, where data reaches the site only when unrelated content ships.

### 3. The public beacon token — commit it, or keep `build_vars`?

The design's D3 argues each site should commit its Cloudflare Web Analytics token directly and delete the injection machinery: the token ships to every visitor in the page, so the repo variable protects nothing, and what it buys (rotation without a commit; forks not inheriting live analytics) is thin against a config key, an exporter, a drift guard, a placeholder convention and a per-repo injection script.

The fleet has since answered the other way in practice — #729's `build_vars` is merged and live on EdFringeNow. It is a well-built mechanism and strictly better than the wholesale export it replaced (#626, closed): a declared list keeps repo vocabulary out of the copy-verbatim stubs, fail-on-unset stops a deleted variable from silently shipping a beaconless site, and being handed only the `vars` context means a secret structurally cannot reach the build.

The design still recommends D3, on the grounds that `build_vars` can carry *only* non-secret values by construction — and any value safe to put in a repo variable is safe to commit — so every possible use of the key has a simpler equivalent in source. **If D3 is accepted, a follow-on question:** retire the `build_vars` capability from the pack once its only user is gone, or keep it dormant for a future build-time value that genuinely varies per environment?

{"number":276,"title":"Move chrome-extension-release plumbing out of core `.github/` into the pack (vendored into consumers)","body":"Resolves the **RELEASE** item of #270: the reusable release workflows (`.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml` + `deploy-privacy-page.yml`) and the three composite actions (`read-release-config`, `bump-extension-patch`, `report-failure`) live in Claudinite's core tree but exist solely for the `chrome-extension-release` pack. They must move behind the pack that owns them, leaving Claudinite with no release-specific GitHub Actions.

## Decision (agreed with owner)

- **Hosting model: vendor into each consumer.** GitHub only resolves reusable workflows/composite actions from a repo's own `.github/`, never from a `packs/…` subdir, so "into the pack" means the pack holds the templates and each consumer hosts a *managed* copy in its own `.github/`. Consumers become self-contained; baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct. This reverses the original "thin consumer" design — deliberately.
- **Phase-2 deletion: automatic, telemetry-gated.** Once the fleet census confirms every consumer has vendored, the census deletes Claudinite's release plumbing automatically as part of migration retirement — no follow-up PR.
- **Secrets: nothing to migrate.** The four `CHROME_*` secrets already live in each consumer repo (they travel via `secrets: inherit` from the consumer's own workflow); Claudinite holds none.

## Plan

1. **Pack = source of truth.** Move the 4 workflows + 3 composite actions into `packs/chrome-extension-release/` as vendored templates; rewrite cross-repo `uses: missingbulb/Claudinite/.github/…@main` → local `uses: ./.github/…`; rename to avoid the in-repo filename collision (the orchestrator and the create-package reusable are both `chrome-extension-release.yml` today).
2. **Migration is the fix vehicle.** A new baseline migration carries: (a) a **materialize** op — baselining writes the vendored set into each consumer's `.github/` and drops the old thin-stub `@main` refs; (b) a **legacyPresent** probe ("still references `missingbulb/Claudinite/.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*`") for fleet telemetry; (c) a **retire-deletes-from-home** list — Claudinite's own release files. Extend the migration mechanism (today rename-only) with the materialize op, and teach the census to delete the home-repo files on retirement.
3. **Tolerant checks during transition.** The `cer/*` checks accept both the old thin-stub shape and the new vendored shape until the migration retires, so no consumer's check suite goes red mid-flight.
4. **Docs.** Update `RELEASE.md`, `.github/workflows/README.md` (drop the frozen-`@main`-API section), and the pack fingerprint.

## Prerequisite for the automatic cut

The automatic phase-2 deletion needs `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` granted **Contents-write on the home repo** — #239 notes this is not granted yet. Until it is, the census logs "grant FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN Contents write" and Claudinite's copies stay in place (harmless — consumers already run off their vendored copies by then).

# Website release flows — alignment design

Status: **proposed** (owner review pending). Refs #722.
Inputs: [COMPARISON.md](COMPARISON.md) (the fleet evidence), [SOUNDNESS.md](SOUNDNESS.md)
(the independent soundness analysis). The subject is the `static-website` pack — merged in
#611 — and the three site repos' bespoke flows it is meant to replace.

> **State note (2026-08-09, evening).** After this design was written, canon merged #729
> (`build_vars`) and EdFringeNow adopted the pack (#319) — see the state updates in
> COMPARISON.md and SOUNDNESS.md. Per the owner's instruction, that movement is treated
> as *data, not as the desired outcome*: this design's conclusions stand where they
> disagree with what shipped. Decisions affected by the new state say so inline.

## Goal

One github-pages-serving standard, owned by the pack, with:

- **no bespoke release mechanism left in any site repo** — the bespoke deploy workflows,
  bump scripts and CI variants all go;
- **minimum GitHub Actions surface** — YAML only where the platform forces it (triggers,
  permissions, OIDC, the Pages actions); all logic in scripts the ordinary vendoring
  converges. The rule of thumb the owner stated holds: a step that needs a secret or the
  repo token must run in Actions; nothing else has to;
- **minimum manual repo settings** — a fresh repo that declares the pack releases on the
  first push, with the custom domain as the only genuinely manual item;
- **customization without forks** — everything repo-specific in `.github/site.config`;
  the workflows stay copy-verbatim.

The acceptance probe (owner-specified): purge every release-related aspect *and setting*
from MissingBulbWebsite so it simulates a new repo, adopt the pack, and the first release
must work on the first go.

## Decisions

### D1. Keep one pack; reshape `static-website` in place

The consolidation policy survives the soundness review intact — one vendored standard,
repo-specifics in a small explicit config. The pack is reworked in place; with EdFringeNow
now adopted (#319), the reshape carries one live adopter's vendored copies along — a
normal converge plus one agent-stage handoff for its workflow files, small and bounded,
rather than the zero-cost rework the original draft assumed. The pack keeps its
`static-website` id (it owns
versioning and CI, not just serving); renaming to `github-pages-serving` is possible but
buys nothing the id doesn't already say — owner's call, recorded as an open question.

What survives unchanged from #611: the `v<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` scheme (it fixes the bespoke
`mmdd` year-boundary flaw), the 5-key `site.config` with no defaults, the additive publish
set with its two loud guards, release-due-by-tag, the ordered check → verify → bump →
Release → deploy stages, and the adoption interview (which is what forces EdFringeNow's
root-publish conversation).
---
# Website release flows — comparison

Status: analysis input for the alignment design ([DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md); soundness review
in [SOUNDNESS.md](SOUNDNESS.md)). Surveys how the
three static-site repos — **EdFringeNow**, **ClaudiniteWebsite**, **MissingBulbWebsite** —
released as of the original survey (2026-08-09, morning), against the canon `static-website`
pack (merged in #611). **The fleet moved the same day** — see
[State update](#state-update-2026-08-09-evening) at the end; the survey body below is kept
as the record of the bespoke era it analyzed.

## The short version

All three repos run the **same hand-copied release flow** with local drift: a Pages deploy
workflow triggered on every push to `main` that bumps a `1.<mmdd>.<n>` version via a copied
`scripts/bump-version.mjs`, commits the bump back with `[skip ci]` and a rebase-retry loop,
sed-injects a Cloudflare analytics token from a repo variable, and uploads an artifact to
GitHub Pages. None cuts a tag or GitHub Release. Each repo also carries its own CI workflow
with a different notion of what CI is.

The canon already owns a standard for exactly this — the `static-website` pack — but it has

1	// The maintenance mechanism is renamed `updates` → `versioned` (#768).
2	//
3	// The mechanism and the task that runs it were one letter apart — `mechanism:
4	// "updates"` and `FORCE_TASKS=update` — and they appear together, in the same
5	// declaration and the same dispatch UI. `versioned` is what the design has called
6	// this scheme all along ("versioned updates"), and `update` stays the task's name,
7	// which is right for a thing a repo DOES.
8	//
9	// WHY A RECORD AND NOT A CONVERGE. The mechanism is a DECLARATION: the repo's own
10	// statement about how it wants to be maintained, in the file the repo owns. Nothing
11	// in the update flows rewrites a member's declaration wholesale — deliberately, since
12	// that file also holds the pack list, the answers to adoption interviews and every
13	// reviewed `accept`. So the rename travels the way declaration changes are supposed
14	// to: one version-ranged record, applied once, idempotent thereafter.
15	//
16	// THE ENGINE STILL ANSWERS TO BOTH NAMES while this record drains
17	// (engine/served-by.mjs, `LEGACY_MECHANISM`). A member reads its own declaration with
18	// the engine it currently has, which is one cycle behind this record — so if the old
19	// spelling stopped parsing the moment the record landed, a correctly-declared repo
20	// would read as `invalid` for exactly one cycle and be reported as misdeclared. The
21	// vocabulary loses `updates` a release later, once no member carries it.
22	export default {
23	  id: 'mechanism-versioned',
24	  landed: '2026-08-13',
25	  version: 2,
26	  summary: 'maintenance.mechanism renamed "updates" → "versioned"; the engine serves both names while this drains',
27	
28	  // A literal, and one of the rare declaration changes where a literal is honest:
29	  // every member's `maintenance` block is written by the same automation, so the
30	  // exact text is shared across the fleet in a way pack lists and interview answers
31	  // never are. `rewrite` preserves the rest of the file byte for byte, which matters
32	  // more here than anywhere — this file carries every reviewed exception the repo has.
33	  rewrite: [{
34	    file: '.claudinite-checks.json',
35	    replace: [{ from: '"mechanism": "updates"', to: '"mechanism": "versioned"' }],
36	  }],
37	
38	  // …and the half no rewrite can do. THE FIRST RECORD TO DECLARE THIS (#798): the
39	  // deterministic op above moves the declaration, and a member's OWN prose is where
40	  // the old name also lives — a README describing how the repo is maintained, a local
41	  // pack's rules, a comment in a workflow, an issue template. The canon cannot know
42	  // where those are, because they are member-authored and it has never seen them.
43	  //
44	  // This is exactly the boundary the apply stage exists on, and it is worth noting
45	  // what it is NOT: it is not "the rename might have missed something" — the rewrite
46	  // is exhaustive over the declaration. It is that the same word means something in
47	  // this repo's own writing, and only a reader of that writing can judge it.
48	  applyStage: {
49	    why: 'the mechanism rename meets whatever this repo wrote about how it is maintained',
50	    instructions: [
51	      'The deterministic half already renamed `maintenance.mechanism` in',
52	      '`.claudinite-checks.json`. Sweep this repo\'s OWN prose for the old name and',
53	      'update it where it refers to the maintenance mechanism: READMEs, local packs',
54	      'under `.claudinite/local/`, CONTRIBUTING notes, workflow comments.',
55	      '',
56	      'Two things to leave alone. The word "update" as a task id (`FORCE_TASKS=update`,',
57	      '`basics/update`) is unchanged and correct — only the MECHANISM was renamed, and',
58	      'the near-collision between the two is the reason it was. And anything under',
59	      '`.claudinite/shared/` is the vendored mount: it is replaced wholesale by the',
60	      'update flows and is never edited in a member.',
61	      '',
62	      'A repo that never wrote about its own maintenance needs nothing here, and that',
63	      'is the common case — converge to a no-op rather than inventing a mention.',
64	    ].join('\n'),
65	  },
66	};
67

1	# Versioned updates — design
2	
3	Status: **agreed** (owner decisions recorded in §10; settled in the
4	2026-08-12 design conversation). Supersedes, once migrated, the unified
5	**baselining** task (`packs/basics/tasks/baselining/`) — its nightly
6	converge-everything-at-canon-head model, its date-held stamp, and its
7	four-condition agent escalation. The phased rollout is tracked as a
8	migration-plan issue (linked from the PR that lands this doc).
9	
10	Terminology decision (owner): the mechanism is called **update** — engine
11	update, pack update, install. The words *baseline / baselining /
12	rebaselining / rebasing* retire with the task that carried them.
13	
14	The shape: the canon splits into a **versioned engine** and **versioned
15	packs**, each with its own update flow. The engine update is fully
16	deterministic — no agentic stage, ever. The pack update keeps a bounded
17	agentic stage ("apply the new pack rules to this repo; repair what they
18	break") with one terminal escape hatch: any non-green end state leaves the
19	PR open, tagged `need-human`. Installing a pack is the same runner as
20	updating one, started from version zero.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 1. Why the current mechanism has an agentic stage at all
25	
26	The census (2026-08-12, this repo's full history — no migration record has
27	ever been deleted, so the population is complete): **three agentic notes
28	ever written**, across eleven migration records, plus three structural
29	escalation conditions in `worker.mjs`'s `escalation()`:
30	
31	| Residual | Cause | Lands in |
32	|---|---|---|
33	| `pack-independence` note | engine composition contract | member local packs |
34	| `prework-rename` note | engine field rename | member local packs |
35	| `fleet-baseline-task` note | pack lever conversion | member `.github/workflows/` |
36	| `withheld-workflows` | credential (Action token cannot write `.github/workflows/`) | — |
37	| `selftest-failed` / `checks-not-green` | judgment: is a non-green converge safe to merge? | — |
38	| executor-routine verification | the CCR routine is invisible to Actions | — |
39	
40	The lesson that shapes this design: the residuals split by **type**
41	(credential / judgment / member-content adaptation), not by which half of
42	the corpus changed. Two of the three notes were engine-caused but landed in
43	member-authored local packs the canon has never seen. So the split below
44	does not *eliminate* those types — it **relocates each to the one flow that
45	can absorb it**, and constrains the engine so its flow needs none of them.
46	
47	## 2. The engine: versioned, cloned, never agentic
48	
49	1. **The engine has running versions.** A release is a qualified snapshot
50	   (the live canary rehearsal runs against it once, per release, instead of
51	   the fleet discovering breakage per repo per night).
52	2. **The update procedure clones the engine release into the repo's mount**
53	   — wholesale replacement, as `compute-vendor-set` does today. The engine's
54	   own files never need migration; they are replaced.
55	3. **Engine migrations cover the member-owned files that reference engine
56	   surfaces** (hooks in `.claude/settings.json`, paths in local-pack code,
57	   the declaration file). They are **usually regex-replace rules, rarely
58	   code — never agentic** (owner decision). **The vendoring flow fetches
59	   only the migrations above the repo's installed engine version** (owner
60	   decision) — the version replaces today's date-based recency window
61	   (`recordDirIsRecent`) as the fetch predicate: an up-to-date repo
62	   vendors none, a lagging repo vendors exactly its gap. Because the same
63	   window currently also drives `migrationActive()` — the legacy-tolerance
64	   predicate consumer checks consult — that tolerance becomes
65	   version-based in the same move ("tolerate the legacy shape while
66	   installed version < N"), or checks would flag legacy shapes on repos
67	   that simply have not updated yet. The discipline this imposes on
68	   engine evolution is accepted and explicit: an engine contract change must
69	   either be mechanically expressible (regex or a small deterministic
70	   codemod shipped with the release) or remain backward-compatible, with the
71	   legacy shape accepted and normalized at load — the posture
72	   `prework-rename` already took. A contract change that satisfies neither
73	   **does not ship** until it does. There is no agentic lane to fall back
74	   on, by construction.
75	4. **The engine update does not write `.github/workflows/`.** The rare
76	   engine change that must touch a workflow file ships as a **custom
77	   update** — an explicitly named, separately credentialed operation (the
78	   Action token structurally cannot write there; the custom update runs
79	   under an MCP-credentialed session or a human). Naming it keeps the lane
80	   from becoming an invisible agentic side door.
81	5. **The engine update merges its PR to main automatically**, gated on the
82	   converged tree passing `selftest --strict` — the gate that exists because
83	   of #555, where an engine change silently stopped every consumer pack from
84	   validating while content checks stayed green. On a red self-test the PR
85	   stays open, tagged `need-human`. A **`force-merge-on-red-ci`** option
86	   (owner decision) overrides the gate for the operator who has judged the
87	   red acceptable — an explicit per-invocation flag, never a stored default.
88	
89	## 3. Packs: versioned, deterministic core, bounded agentic tail
90	
91	6. **Each pack has a version number**, and **each pack version declares the
92	   minimum engine version it requires**, enforced by the updater: a pack
93	   update never applies past the installed engine (§5). This is what makes
94	   the split coherent — the current single-snapshot guarantee ("the set and
95	   the content can never come from different snapshots") is replaced by a
96	   *checkable* compatibility constraint rather than dropped.
97	7. **A pack update is deterministic first**: vendor the new pack version,
98	   run its version-ranged migrations (vN→vN+1, in order), converge wiring.
99	   **Pack migrations live in the pack's own `migrations/` folder** and are
100	   fetched by the same version gate as the engine's (owner decision): only
101	   the records above the repo's installed version of *that pack* ship in
102	   the mount. The flat canon-wide `migrations/` directory does not survive
103	   the split — each record moves to the flow (engine or pack) that owns it.
104	   **Workflow churn belongs to the pack flow, explicitly** (owner decision):
105	   the scheduler workflow's content is a function of the *task set*
106	   (`declaredSecrets` unions `required_secrets` across discovered tasks), so
107	   pack changes are what rewrite it, and the pack flow carries the
108	   credential to land those files — the MCP lane baselining's agent stage
109	   uses today, §2b of its task.
110	8. **A pack update may carry an agentic stage**: "apply the new pack rules —
111	   fix the repo, repair the tests." This is the one place agentic work
112	   survives, because it is the one residual no mechanism can absorb: the
113	   pack's new rules meet member-authored content the canon has never seen.
114	   The stage also inherits the orphaned **executor-routine verification**
115	   (the CCR routine that fires on `ready-for-agent` is not a GitHub
116	   artifact; only an agent session can see it, and this is the only agent
117	   lane left).
118	
119	   **The word is *may*, and the RECORDS are what decide it** (#798). A pack
120	   record declares `applyStage: { why, instructions }`; an update whose gap
121	   holds no such record is delivered without a session. The first
122	   implementation asked the version plan instead — "any declared pack whose
123	   version moved" — and that is a fact about the *canon* where the stage
124	   needs a fact about the *member*. Because a record can only reach an
125	   up-to-date member if its pack's manifest bumps (§3.7), and every bump
126	   summoned a session, **a purely mechanical migration could not be shipped
127	   without spending an agent session on every member in the fleet**. The
128	   record's author knows which of the two kinds they wrote; a version number
129	   never can. An **install** stays unconditional (§4) — that genuinely is
130	   first contact.
131	9. **The pack update merges its PR to main** unless it ends non-green.
132	   **Every** non-green terminal — unanswered interview questions, an agentic
133	   repair that leaves checks red, a migration that could not complete —
134	   ends the same way: the PR stays open, the dispatch issue is tagged
135	   `need-human`, the run stops. Interviews are one instance of the rule,
136	   not the rule.
137	
138	## 4. Install = update from version zero
139	
140	Installing a pack is the pack updater started with no prior state: vendor,
141	converge, agentic apply, deliver — the same flow, same terminals (§3.9:
142	interview unanswered → PR open + `need-human`). **An install runs no
143	migrations** (owner decision): the vendored pack content is already the
144	newest shape, so there is no older state to migrate — replaying history
145	onto a fresh install is both wasted work and a correctness hazard
146	(migrations assume the shapes their era produced, not an empty repo).
147	The install stamps the pack's **latest** version directly; migrations are
148	exclusively for repos that were installed at an older one. Two
149	install-specific provisions:
150	
151	- **One-shot seed ops.** Some install effects are seeded once and owned by
152	  the repo thereafter (the README badge row is the existing precedent:
153	  seeded by `--badges` at adoption, never re-converged, precisely so
154	  updates cannot rewrite a member's README). The install carries an
155	  **initial migration** — ordinary code the runner executes, not a "real"
156	  migration — and the mechanism marks these ops *run-once-at-install*.
157	  The updater must never re-run them; the distinction between *seeded*
158	  (repo-owned from then on) and *converged* (rewritten every update)
159	  surfaces is load-bearing.
160	- The interview happens through the same open-PR + `need-human` terminal,
161	  which degrades gracefully to async — better than today's adopt-pack
162	  skill, which needs a live session.
163	
164	## 5. Invariants
165	
166	- **No agentic work in the engine flow.** Ever. The escape hatches are the
167	  named custom update (workflows) and the `need-human` terminal (red
168	  self-test) — both visible, neither a model.
169	- **Version-ranged migrations replace the date stamp.** "Which migrations
170	  apply" becomes "installed version → target version," retiring the
171	  held-stamp subtleties (#329, #330). The same range gates **fetching**:
172	  a mount carries exactly the migration records in its gap, none on an
173	  up-to-date repo, and a fresh install carries — and runs — none at all.
174	- **Compatibility is enforced, not assumed**: pack min-engine-version
175	  checked before apply; violation is a `need-human` terminal, not a guess.
176	- **Every non-green terminal looks the same**: PR open, `need-human`,
177	  stop. No flow merges red — except the engine's explicit
178	  `force-merge-on-red-ci`, which is an operator's signed judgment, not a
179	  flow default.
180	- **A repo that reports a clean update is clean.** The withholding pattern
181	  (paths silently dropped from a push, forever) does not survive: what a
182	  flow cannot write, it either hands to the flow that can (workflows → pack
183	  lane / custom update) or surfaces as `need-human`.
184	
185	  In practice this means the pack flow **stages** `.github/workflows/`
186	  content at `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` — a path its Action token
187	  *can* push — and ends at `apply-stage` until a session with an MCP
188	  credential moves it into place. Three properties, and the design needs all
189	  three: nothing is dropped (the update does not report clean while owing a
190	  file), the content is **reviewable** (it lands in the update's own PR diff,
191	  where a human sees the workflow change before any session touches it), and
192	  it is **recoverable** (a session that never ran leaves the content on the
193	  branch rather than losing it with a request file). The staging directory is
194	  swept every cycle, so it is empty exactly when nothing is owed — which is
195	  also what makes "did the apply stage actually run" a question with an
196	  answer (#797, #649).
197	
198	## 6. What this retires
199	
200	- The `baselining` task (task.md, task.mjs, worker.mjs), its escalation
201	  codes, and its dispatch-issue protocol.
202	- The `agentic:` field on migration records: engine migrations may not
203	  carry it at all; pack migrations express agentic work as the pack
204	  update's apply stage instead, by declaring `applyStage: { why,
205	  instructions }` (§3.8). What the successor drops is the **model** knob —
206	  which model runs a session is the scheduler's answer, off the task
207	  declaration, and a record naming its own was a second authority over the
208	  same fact.
209	- The date-held stamp (`claudinite.updated` gating note application).
210	- The baselining vocabulary, corpus-wide.
211	
212	## 7. Known-open
213	
214	- The `local-pack-namespace` declaration rewrite (bare id → `local/<id>`)
215	  remains unowned; the versioned scheme should place it in an engine
216	  migration (it is a regex on the declaration file — squarely within §2.3).
217	- Escalation-frequency measurement across the fleet (which `escalation()`
218	  codes actually fire) would validate the split's cost model; nice to have
219	  before Phase 2, not a blocker.
220	
221	## 8. Propagation and session access
222	
223	**Member repos change nothing by hand, and their local packs change not at
224	all.** Local packs are repo-owned, not distributed: under this scheme they
225	get no version numbers, no `migrations/` folders, and no install flow, and
226	the cutover never rewrites them. The one indirect touch is
227	`migrationActive()` tolerance moving from date-based to version-based —
228	shipped together with the fetch gate (§2.3) so a lagging repo's local
229	packs keep their legacy-shape tolerance until that repo actually updates.
230	A local pack's adaptation remains what it is today: a conformance finding
231	resolved in the repo's own sessions, never a step of this migration.
232	
233	The member-side deltas the migration does produce are all written by the
234	flows themselves: new stamp fields in `.claudinite-checks.json`
235	(installed engine version, per-pack versions, the which-mechanism rollout
236	flag), the relocated migration records inside the vendored mount, and
237	eventually the new worker.
238	
239	**Implementation happens in the canon repo alone** — no fleet-scoped
240	session is required. The propagation channel already exists and is
241	self-carrying: the vendored worker shallow-clones fresh canon every cycle
242	and executes the *cloned* canon's vendoring, wiring, and migration
243	scripts as subprocesses, never its own stale copies (worker.mjs:14–25,
244	51–54). New vendor-set logic, the per-pack migration layout, and the
245	version gate are live fleet-wide the night after they land in canon;
246	changes to the worker/driver itself lag exactly one cycle (vendored in
247	cycle N, executing in N+1). Three caveats, none requiring fleet access to
248	implement:
249	
250	1. **Scheduler workflow stub changes** land per-repo through the existing
251	   agent lane (baselining §2b's MCP credential; the pack flow's lane after
252	   Phase 2) — automatic, during each repo's own cycle.
253	2. **The CCR executor routines** are the one per-repo artifact outside
254	   GitHub's reach. Their prompt is a thin pointer to the vendored
255	   `executor.md`, so content changes ride the mount; only a change to the
256	   dispatch *wiring* (label name, model, launcher prompt) would need
257	   per-repo trigger-API access. The rollout should avoid requiring that —
258	   or accept the bootstrap-Part-6 owner-issue path where it cannot.
259	3. **The fleet-wide cutover verification** (Phase 5's precondition) is
260	   fleet-scoped, but it belongs to the sheepdog enforcer's existing fleet
261	   tasks — machinery, not an implementation session.
262	
263	## 9. Migration
264	
265	Phased rollout tracked in the migration-plan issue (filed alongside this
266	doc). Summary: version scaffolding first (no behavior change), then the
267	engine flow, then the pack flow, then install, then retirement of
268	baselining and its vocabulary.
269	
270	## 10. Owner decisions recorded
271	
272	1. Engine auto-merge is selftest-gated, **with a `force-merge-on-red-ci`
273	   override** (2026-08-12).
274	2. Workflow churn is **explicitly the pack flow's** (2026-08-12).
275	3. Engine migrations are "usually regex, rarely code" — **no agentic work
276	   on the engine, ever** (2026-08-12).
277	4. `need-human` covers **all** non-green terminals, not only interviews
278	   (2026-08-12).
279	5. Pack versions **declare and enforce** a minimum engine version
280	   (2026-08-12).
281	6. The mechanism is named **update**; baselining vocabulary retires
282	   (2026-08-12).
283	7. Migration fetching is **version-gated**: vendoring ships only the
284	   records above the repo's installed version — engine and pack alike —
285	   replacing the date-based recency window (2026-08-12).
286	8. Pack migrations live in **each pack's own `migrations/` folder**; the
287	   flat canon-wide directory retires with the split (2026-08-12).
288	9. **An install runs no migrations**: the vendored content is already the
289	   newest shape, and the install stamps the latest version directly
290	   (2026-08-12).
291

{"number":840,"title":"Engine-driven format changes to consumer-held files need a first-class migration class","body":"Owner decision context (2026-08-14, on #564): converting members' local `pack.mjs` files to `pack.json` rides a `basics` pack record with `applyStage` — but the owner flagged the routing itself as the gap: *"this is a classic 'engine changed, the format of local packs should change' migration."*

The gap: the **engine** owns the local-pack manifest format, but the engine flow may carry no agentic work (versioned-updates DESIGN §5), and its declarative ops (`aliases`/`materialize`/`rewrite`/`declarePacks`) cannot express "reshape this member-authored file". So every engine-side format change to a consumer-held file gets routed ad-hoc through whichever pack is convenient (`basics`, because it is declared everywhere) — the same shape as the #555 manifest tightening, which shipped with *no* carrier and broke eleven local packs silently.

Ask: make "the engine changed a format consumers hold" a recognized migration class with a designated carrier — so the record can be authored where the change lives (with the engine), while the member-side session it needs runs through the one agentic lane that exists (the pack flow), without each occurrence re-deriving the routing. `legacyPresent` telemetry and the retirement gate should come with the class, not be re-invented per change.

Closing condition: the next engine-owned format change to a consumer-held file has an obvious, documented place to land, and the pack.json conversion's routing (via `basics`) is either retroactively blessed as that place or superseded by it.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/840","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-14T18:43:43Z","updated_at":"2026-08-14T18:43:43Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

Status note from the #649 verification run; the blocker here is unchanged.

**Still blocked by #239** — the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` Contents-write grant on the home repo. Nothing today touches that, and the four `.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml` files plus the two actions are still in `main`'s `.github/`.

Two things about this issue's *phase 1* did change, though.

**The delivery mechanism this plan rests on has now been proven live.** The plan's step 2 is "a **materialize** op — [the update flow] writes the vendored set into each consumer's `.github/`", and `chrome-release-vendoring` has carried exactly that since #280. But a record materializing into `.github/workflows/` had **never actually run against a live member** — that is the residual #649 was reopened for and the last open item on #768. Until today, phase 1 was landed code whose delivery step was untested; if it had been broken, the first consumer to converge would have failed its whole update, not just that file (the Action token's refusal rejects the entire ref).

Verified end to end on the canary on 2026-08-14 (evidence on #649): the record's write is withheld to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, rides the PR as a reviewable added file, the update parks at `apply-stage`, and a session moves it into `.github/workflows/` byte-for-byte. So `chrome-release-vendoring` should now be expected to deliver when its consumers converge.

**The vocabulary here is stale.** This issue says "baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct" and "baselining materializes it". Baselining was retired in #768 phase 5; the owner is now the pack update flow (`updates/pack-update.mjs`), and the materialize reaches `.github/workflows/` through the withhold lane rather than by direct push — which is precisely why it could not simply be pushed in the first place.
