{"number":564,"title":"Pack manifests as JSON: pack.json + pack.schema.json, code split into sibling files","body":"Owner comment (process-change): "Why are packs declared using mjs? Is it just the `detect` part? It seems they can all be just JSON declarations, and if we have some code that detects, we can put that in a different file. And once it's just JSON — can't you declare the schema in a nicer way than `engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs`? You can still have validations (a simple unit test) for making sure all the skills/rules are declared and there's no drift, but at least the files will be sane."

Measured across the 29 manifests (27 canon + the home's 2 local packs): **988 lines, 56 of them `import` statements, 350 of them comments.** Almost nothing in a `pack.mjs` needs to be code.

## What is actually code today

| Field | Packs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `detect` | 13 (14 declare `null`) | ~10 are one-liners over `ctx.tracked` — `includes`, `endsWith`, a path regex, or the shared `hasMarkerNearRoot` helper — all expressible as data. **3 need real logic**: `chrome-extension` (locates the extension manifest), `chrome-extension-release` (recognizes a release orchestrator workflow), `leaflet` (scans file *content*). |
| `worldRules` / `workRules` | all | Code only as *imports*. In JSON these become filenames the loader imports. |
| `env` | 2 | Genuinely code — `setup`/`probe` are functions of the pack's config returning shell. |
| `contributes` / `contributedRules` | 3 / 1 | `contributes` is a map of pack id → rule modules, so filenames. `contributedRules` (barriers only) is a real seam. |
| everything else | — | Pure data: `id`, `badge`, `marker`, `prose`, `seededByDefault`, `requires`, `ruleRoutingGuidance`, `skills`, `questions`. |

## Shape wanted

- `packs//pack.json` for all 29, with `$schema` pointing at a `pack.schema.json`.
- Optional sibling code files, named from the JSON, only where needed: `detect.mjs` (3 packs), `env.mjs` (2), `contributed-rules.mjs` (1).
- Rules referenced **by filename**, which buys a drift guard the current shape cannot have: every rule `.mjs` in the pack directory must appear in exactly one of the two scope lists. Today an undeclared rule module is simply invisible.

## Why it is worth more than tidiness

**The loader stops executing arbitrary code at load.** Today a consumer's local `pack.mjs` is `import()`ed during SessionStart in every session and on every check run — which is precisely why `pack-registry.mjs` carries per-pack import isolation. With JSON, the ~26 packs that need no code execute none.

**A real schema.** `pack.schema.json` gives editor autocomplete and validation that `PACK_FIELDS` never will.

## What it costs

1. **The 350 comment lines have nowhere to go** — and they are real rationale, not noise: why `basics` requires `barriers` and contributes the isolation barrier as manifest data, why `canon-curation`'s declaration cardinality is what makes its tasks central-once. The natural home is the pack README, which is now exactly the "rationale the manifest cannot carry" file after #559 — this brings two or three of the deleted ones back.
2. **`pack.mjs` is a consumer-held shape**, not only ours — every member repo has local packs. Needs both-shapes tolerance plus a baseline migration to retire the old one, per `consumer-safe-changes.md`.

## Scope note on validation

A consumer's local pack must be validated at *their* Stop hook, not this repo's CI, so loader-side validation stays. JSON Schema replaces the **field-shape** half of `pack-schema.mjs`; the **cross-file drift guards** (skills ↔ directory, rules ↔ files) remain loader checks with unit tests over them. Net effect: that module shrinks substantially rather than disappearing.

{"number":748,"title":"conformance-backlog: committed-build-artifact check (promote cannot land a check — fixtures sit outside its write surface)","body":"Two things, from the 2026-08-11 `canon-curation/growth-promote` run (#745, PR #747).

## 1. A structural block: promote's ladder cannot reach the check rung

`growth-promote`'s task spec says a lesson a check can carry is **authored as the check** in the promote PR — "the rule module in the right pack, the failure message carrying the generalized lesson, **plus a fixture test proving it fires**".

That is mechanically impossible today:

- promote's write surface is bounded to `packs/` and `skills/`, enforced by `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/promote-scope.mjs` on the `growth-promote` branch prefix;
- a canon pack's fixture test lives under `packs-tests/`, which is **outside** that surface;
- and it cannot move into `packs/` either — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins a closed set of test roots (`engine-tests/`, `packs-tests/`, `vendoring/`, `dev/tools/`, `.claudinite/local/packs/`), with `engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs` failing on any tracked test outside them.

So every promote run must fall back to prose for a convertible rule, and the "prose is the fallback, not the default" ladder never fires. Whichever way it is resolved (widen `inBounds` to `packs-tests/`, or add `packs/` as a test root), it is an owner decision — the run declined to widen its own gate.

## 2. The conversion this blocked

The `.gitignore`-pruning lesson (LaughCounter's local pack, promoted as prose to `git-github-advanced` in #747) converts to a world-scope `basics` check. Written and green locally before being pulled:

- **`packs/basics/committed-build-artifact.mjs`** — advisory, relevance-first. Flags a *tracked* file matching a confined set of artifacts no project tracks on purpose: `__pycache__/`, `*.py[co]`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `*.egg-info/`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`. The `fix` line carries the lesson (delete the artifacts before dropping their ignore rules; read `git diff --cached --stat` after a bulk `git add -A`).
- **`packs-tests/basics/committed-build-artifact.test.mjs`** — four cases: clean tree silent; a swept-in `__pycache__` found; the tool-cache/OS set found; and a narrowness case proving silence on deliberately vendored trees (`node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`) and on prose merely naming `__pycache__`.

Advisory rather than blocking on purpose: the fix is a deletion, and pre-existing junk in a member repo should surface as a finding to clear, not red that repo's sweep and block its maintenance PR.

The set was chosen so the check stays inert on anything a repo might legitimately vendor; `node_modules/` and `dist/` are deliberately excluded.

Refs #745.

**The problem:** a major task has two artifacts — a source-controlled design/migration plan and a GitHub tracking issue with a `- [ ]`/`- [x]` checklist (the "read status and pick up the work" point). When a phase lands, the committed plan's status is updated in the same PR (the diff forces review), but the issue checklist is a separate surface no diff touches, so it silently drifts. Already live: `per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md` says Phase 1 is "same day, no soak" while #394's Phase 1 item still says "Soak ~1 week."

**The design, in two surfaces:**
1. **In-session (timely):** a transcript-only post-merge check-the-work rule — `in-session-github-access` (blocking) means in-session code has no GitHub REST credential, so the rule reads the merge, the tracker discovery, and the post-merge checklist edit from the session transcript's MCP tool calls. Enablers: `work.mergedThisSession()` and a Stop-hook post-merge trigger (the merge recipe leaves a clean tree, which would otherwise fast-exit).
2. **Nightly (convergent):** plans state, per phase, *how completion is decided* — a checklist item may carry `` naming a dependency-free Node script whose **exit 0 means the phase is done** ("if this code passes, phase 3 is done"); no marker ⇒ the phase's prose **Verify** block in the plan doc is the criteria. The `plan-status-update` task (daily, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue) re-derives every tracker's checklist from these verifiers — flipping what sessions missed, flagging (never auto-un-flipping) a checked item whose code verifier now fails.

**Invariant:** any open `plan-tracking` issue must carry a todo checklist and have a box **flipped** in the same session as each merge that advances it (after the merge, not before — an item isn't done until it's on `main`). The issue *count* is not enforced.

**Phases (detail in the design doc):**
- [ ] **Convention + seed** — define the `plan-tracking` label and its meaning in the `grow_with_claudinite` / merge docs; apply it to existing in-flight tracker(s) (#394).
- [ ] **Primitive + trigger** — `work.mergedThisSession()` (transcript-derived accepted PRs) and the Stop hook's post-merge trigger, each with red-first tests.
- [ ] **Verifier (in-session)** — the `plan-tracking-freshness` rule in `grow_with_claudinite`; fires when a merge happened with no post-merge checklist flip, quiet otherwise.
- [ ] **Recipe wiring** — `merge-to-main` gains the "sync the `plan-tracking` issue after the merge" step (prose asks; the check guarantees).
- [ ] **Docs** — the convention in the pack README; design-doc status box; this issue points at the doc.
- [ ] **Per-phase verifiers (convention)** — `` code verifiers (exit 0 ⇒ done) with prose Verify blocks as fallback; recorded in the pack README and the nightly worker doc.
- [ ] **Nightly status update** — the `plan-status-update` task (daily/sonnet/none, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue): re-verifies each tracker, flips passes, flags regressions in a comment.

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left).

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left).

{"number":498,"title":"scheduler-workflow-shape should validate the scopes a repo's tasks actually need, not a fixed two","body":"Surfaced by the `growth-extract` run on #484, and pulled out of that run's RULES.md entries during review: this reads as a proposed mechanism change rather than a rule a session can follow, so filing it here instead.

## The gap

`packs/basics/scheduler-workflow-shape.mjs` validates exactly two permissions on a repo's `claudinite-scheduler.yml`, both hard-coded:

```
if (!/^\s*contents:\s*write\b/m.test(text))       → flag
if (!/^\s*pull-requests:\s*write\b/m.test(text))  → flag
```

Those two cover baselining's `deliver()` (push a branch, open a PR, arm auto-merge). They cover nothing a *task's worker* needs. So a task whose worker calls a GitHub endpoint requiring some third scope passes the check with a stub that never granted it, and the failure lands at runtime in a member repo.

## How it actually bit (#478)

`store-release`'s worker POSTs a `workflow_dispatch`, which needs `actions: write`. The stub granted `actions: read`. Every fire 403'd, the worker exited 1, and the scheduler converged the task to `needs-human` — leaving three cut-over members with no working release path. Nothing caught it earlier because nothing was looking: the check validates a fixed pair, and the next task needing a fourth scope will land exactly the same way.

## Suggested direction

Make the required scope set *derived* rather than fixed. Roughly:

1. Let a task declare what its worker needs in its `task.mjs` — e.g. `required_scopes: ['actions:write']` — alongside the existing `agent_model` / `expected_outcome` fields, validated by `task-contract.mjs`.
2. Have `scheduler-workflow-shape` union the declared scopes across the repo's enabled tasks with the baselining floor (`contents:write`, `pull-requests:write`) and assert the workflow grants each one, naming the task that needs it in the failure message.
3. Have the stub generator emit the union, so a repo that adopts a task gets the grant with it rather than hand-editing `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml`.

That turns "read the scope off the endpoint and grant it yourself, and hope you remembered" into a declaration the check enforces. Worth weighing against the simpler option — keep the check fixed but widen the floor to include `actions: write` — which costs a broader default token but no new contract surface.

Not started; opening for a decision on which direction (or neither) before any implementation.

{"number":394,"title":"Implement per-project maintenance scheduling (owner-orchestrated rollout)","body":"Implementation tracker for the per-project scheduling conversion. Design + plan merged in #391 (Refs #390).

**Read first (on `main`):**
- Design — [`docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md)
- Migration plan — [`docs/per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md)

**End state (DESIGN §8):** every repo schedules itself via a vendored hourly scheduler Action (the repo's only cron; hashed minute :10–:50) that evaluates per-task code preconditions and dispatches agent work as `[claudinite-task]` issues labeled `ready-for-agent`; a per-repo executor CCR routine fired by that label event runs each task at its declared model. `run_daily/` → `tasks//{task.mjs,task.md}`; `.claudinite/local_packs/` → `.claudinite/local/packs/` (declaration token `local/`). Fleet-scoped work (promote, discover-packs, migrations-retire, prose-to-checks, census) becomes ordinary tasks of the canon/sheepdog repos; baselining+migrations-apply become a per-repo basics self-refresh.

**Orchestration rules:** the owner drives each phase in a session; this rollout does **not** go through the regular migration-notes mechanism; the old central routine + the two GCEC triggers stay live (and are the rollback) until Phase 4; the `schedule` key in `.claudinite-checks.json` is the per-repo cutover marker, so exactly one mechanism owns a repo at any time.

**Phases (detail in MIGRATION.md):**
- [x] **Phase 0 — canon groundwork:** build `engine/scheduler/`; add `schedule` to `CONFIG_KEYS`; `local_packs`→`local/packs` (dual-root scan) + rename the canon's own; convert canon pack tasks (baselining → per-repo self-refresh, store-release → absorbs the release cron); new/rescoped checks; doc rewrites; the `schedule`-key transition guard. No behavior change until a repo declares `schedule`.
- [x] **Phase 1 — GCEC pilot:** vendor-refresh, scheduler workflow, strip the release cron, labels, move both `dev/routines/` into the gcec pack as `tasks/`, port the create-extractor triage *decision* into the precondition (fetch/scaffold stay in the task), write the `schedule` key, create the label-wired executor routine, disable the two old GCEC triggers. Soak ~1 week.
- [x] **Phase 2 — canon cutover:** canon-side tasks (promote `daily`, discover-packs `weekly`, migrations-retire `daily+1h`, prose-to-checks `daily`), `fleet` signal over `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`, sheepdog `fleet-census` task; canon repo gets its own scheduler + executor.
- [ ] **Phase 3 — remaining 9 consumers** (EdFringeNow, gRatio, TLDR, HelloWorldFlutterApp, EdFringeAllocator, CrosswordChat, Sheepdog, LaughCounter, ShoutsAndWhispers), batched ~3 at a time.
- [ ] **Phase 4 — decommission:** delete the central CCR trigger + both disabled GCEC triggers; remove `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `routines/fleet/`; drop the transition guard, `run_daily`/`local_packs` aliases; retire enrollment; final boxed review vs DESIGN §8.

**Independent fix (ship anytime, not gated on a phase):** `engine/pack_loader/inject-pack-prose.mjs` imports `registry.mjs` but the file is `pack-registry.mjs` — active packs' RULES.md are silently not injected at SessionStart, fleet-wide. One-line fix + regression test + vendor refresh.

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left).

{"number":723,"title":"Website release flows: comparison and alignment design","body":"Refs #722.

Analysis-and-design work for aligning EdFringeNow, ClaudiniteWebsite and MissingBulbWebsite on one github-pages-serving standard. All three deliverables are in `docs/website-release-flows/`:

- **COMPARISON.md** — the three bespoke flows side by side (the hand-copied core, the drift, the genuinely project-specific parts, the shared design flaws), against the canon `static-website` pack (#611).
- **SOUNDNESS.md** — an independent review-agent analysis: verified platform facts (GITHUB_TOKEN push semantics, `permissions:` overriding the repo default, `enablement: true`, `vars` reach, the release-baseline traps) and eight ranked findings, the top two being that release-on-push is blind to workflow-authored pushes and that the pack's release semantics don't fit EdFringeNow's hourly data churn.
- **DESIGN.md** — the proposed corrections: reshape the pack in place to **two thin workflow shims over pipeline scripts in the vendored mount** (~110 lines of YAML instead of ~890 across 4 workflows + 3 composite actions); commit the public beacon token and delete the injection machinery; self-enable Pages; state the trigger contract (publish-set-writing automation dispatches the release, never relies on push); add a `deploy-only` dispatch mode so data refreshes redeploy without minting Releases; converge failure reporting to one issue; shrink manual repo settings to the custom domain alone. Acceptance probe: purge all release aspects and settings from MissingBulbWebsite to simulate a fresh repo, adopt the pack, and the first release must work on the first go. Ends with the post-design review of #626 and open questions for the owner.

**Updated for the fleet's same-day movement** (recorded as data, not as the desired outcome — the design's conclusions stand where they disagree): canon merged #729 (`build_vars`) and closed #626; EdFringeNow adopted the pack (#319, superseding #207) with an explicit publish set. The update surfaces one live regression: EdFringeNow's hourly data refreshes push with the scheduler's GITHUB_TOKEN, which fires no push workflow — so as merged they land on `main` without deploying, contrary to #319's ~17-releases/day expectation. That makes the design's D5/D6 (automation dispatches; `deploy-only` mode) its most urgent piece. MissingBulbWebsite PR #39 remains open and is now triply stale.

No pack code changes in this PR — design only, implementation follows owner review.

{"number":170,"title":"Revisit: Workflow tool's interactive opt-in blocks unattended routines (waiting on Anthropic)","body":"## The limitation

The multi-agent-orchestration **`Workflow`** tool requires an **interactive human opt-in on every run** ("Allow Claude to run a workflow?"). That prompt only disappears under bypass-permissions / headless modes a scheduler can't be relied on to be in. Because an unattended routine has no human to click **Allow**, any routine that fans out through the Workflow tool stalls on step one.

This also means the tool's nicest ergonomics are off-limits to us for unattended work: committing a Workflow script and having the nightly job just run it by name (`Workflow({name: ...})`) hits the **same** prompt — the gate is on *invoking* a workflow, not on authoring one. And the parallel-agent step can't be pushed into a plain committed script either, since spawning Claude subagents is a harness capability, not something arbitrary code can call.

## Our current workaround

We fan the fleet daily maintenance routine out with **plain subagent dispatch** (the Agent/Task tool) instead, which carries no opt-in gate, and the orchestrator honors the phase barriers itself. See #168 / #169 and `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`.

This works and is the right default (no dependency on an out-of-repo permission-mode setting), but it costs us the Workflow tool's built-in phase/barrier machinery and the option to run committed, reviewed orchestration code.

## Why keep this open

This is a limitation of the platform, not our code — we're **waiting on the world to change**. If Anthropic later lets an unattended session pre-authorize the Workflow tool (a settings allowlist entry, an environment/routine permission mode that reliably suppresses just this prompt, or persisted per-workflow consent that survives a fresh cloud clone), we could reconsider using committed Workflow scripts for the fleet routine and get determinism + review back.

**Action:** periodically check with Anthropic / the Claude Code release notes whether the Workflow tool can be pre-authorized for unattended sessions. When it can, revisit the plain-dispatch decision in the routine spec.

10:- **API Gateway HTTP API (v2) rejects a `chrome-extension://` origin in CORS `AllowOrigins`** with `BadRequestException: Invalid format for origin`, accepting only `http(s)://…` or `*`. An API fronted by a browser-extension (or other non-`http`) origin must therefore set `AllowOrigins: ['*']` and rely on its **JWT authorizer**, not CORS, as the security boundary.
16:- **A custom request header turns even a public GET into a preflighted CORS request.** Any non-simple header (e.g. a client-version header) makes the browser send an `OPTIONS` preflight, so the API's CORS `AllowHeaders` must list that header or the real request is blocked *in the browser* — while server-side unit tests that never run the CORS layer stay green.

Note the plan called these "the two **disabled** GCEC triggers" — they were not disabled, both were `enabled: true`.

**Step 2 — remove the routine and planner. Done** (#473). `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md`, the whole `routines/fleet/` tree, the Phase 0.6 transition guard, the `local_packs` dual-root scan, and the five packs' `run_daily/` folders. `reference-integrity` went 43 blocking → 0. Prose that existed only in the deleted worker docs was moved into the live task docs first — notably `dedup.md`'s **Strips** definition, the only one in the tree, which `dedup-prune-integrity` enforces.

**Step 3 — retire enrollment. Done.** One enrollment issue existed fleet-wide (VascularColoring #1) and is closed. `tasks/baselining/` carries no enrollment step, so the code half retired with `run_daily/`.

**Step 4 — repo-wide sweep. Done** as part of #473.

**Step 5 — final review against DESIGN §8.**

| clause | verdict |
|---|---|
| 1. per-repo scheduler is the repo's only cron, plus one label-fired executor | ✅ **met exactly, all twelve repos** — every minute matches its freshly-computed hash, all inside :10–:50, all carry `taskScheduler`, all have exactly one label-fired executor |
| 2. Claudinite runs §6's four tasks | ⚠️ two of four — `prose-to-checks-sweep` was deliberately relocated to `grow_with_claudinite`; **`growth-discover-packs` (fleet sweep) was never built** |
| 3. deletions | ✅ complete as of step 1 |
| 4. Yestersummary unchanged | ✅ |

Clause 1 was verified by reading every workflow's `on:` block in every repo, not by code search — that search returned zero cron hits for EdFringeNow, which carries seventeen.

- **`growth-discover-packs` (Claudinite-side, fleet)** — DESIGN §6/§8 promise it; nothing provides it, so no one notices a technology used across the fleet with no canon pack. Being built now.

Labeling `quick-win`: scope is exactly the two remaining bullets — (1) fold the comment-stripper copies into one helper with a `preserveOffsets` option and repoint the call sites, (2) add `work.addedKeys(file, atPath)` and repoint the three JSON-diff rules onto it. No new vocabulary, no design questions open — pure consolidation per `docs/declarative-checks/REVIEW.md` §"cheaper wins in the imperative corpus".

1	# Making changes to Claudinite without hurting consumers
2	
3	> **Status: provisional — beliefs, not law.** Every entry here says what we're *currently* doing
4	> and *why we think* it helps. When an entry blocks a better change, challenge the entry rather
5	> than contorting the change; being cited in this guide is not, by itself, a reason something
6	> must stay. We'll solidify entries once they've earned it.
7	
8	Claudinite is vendored into every consuming repo, so a change here lands in many places, on the
9	fleet's schedule, usually with no human watching. This guide collects what we currently believe
10	about making such changes safely. It is a maintainer document for sessions working *in* this
11	repo; it is not part of the vendored corpus.
12	
13	## First, know which channel the change travels
14	
15	Since the fleet moved to the tracked vendored mount (vendoring/DESIGN.md, phases 1–3 complete),
16	the channel model is small — nothing reaches a consumer instantly, and nothing arrives outside
17	its git history:
18	
19	- **The vendored corpus** (`engine/`, `packs/` — checks, prose, bundled skills) — each member
20	  holds a tracked snapshot under `.claudinite/shared/`, converged **whole-set** to the canon
21	  head by the nightly refresh and stamped with its provenance. Propagation lags one nightly,
22	  lands as a reviewable commit on the member's `claudinite/maintenance` PR (auto-merged on
23	  `auto-merge` delivery once the repo's checks pass, held for the owner on `review`), and the
24	  rollback story is the same channel: fix the canon, the next nightly re-heals. A wrong
25	  *blocking* check still fails every member's Stop hook — visible and recoverable, but
26	  fleet-wide noise, so treat check changes as production changes.
27	- **Migration notes** (`engine/migrations/<date>-<slug>/`, or `packs/<pack>/migrations/<date>-<slug>/`) — the channel for anything convergence
28	  can't express: renames of consumer-held wiring, declaration rewrites, one-off agentic steps.
29	  Stamp-day-gated and idempotent; the note's `legacyPresent` telemetry says when the fleet has
30	  moved and (for `retire: 'auto'`) retires the record itself.
31	- **Copied artifacts** (pack `stubs/`, seeded configs) — these do **not** propagate at all. Each
32	  consumer holds its own copy, which drifts silently unless a check enforces its shape. Changing
33	  the source file alone only affects repos bootstrapped *after* the change.
34	- **Bootstrap wiring** (the committed artifacts [bootstrap.md](bootstrap.md) seeds:
35	  `settings.json` hook registrations, the two gitignore lines, the pack declaration) —
36	  propagates through the nightly update's idempotent backfills on the same delivery PR.
37	  The discipline: a change here is written as steps that **converge from every layout in the
38	  wild**, not just from the latest.
39	
40	Out-of-repo state remains the one channel git never reaches: a web environment's pasted Setup
41	script is snapshotted at environment build. A change that moves what the pasted script calls
42	needs the script's own probe to fail fast and a member issue asking for the one human action
43	(re-paste).
44	
45	## Migrating a copied artifact (stubs and the like)
46	
47	Because copies won't move on their own, we currently migrate them through the conformance
48	checks, in one Claudinite-only change:
49	
50	1. Change the source artifact in the pack (the stub under `packs/<pack>/stubs/`).
51	2. Make sure the pack's conformance check enforces the properties that changed, with a `fix`
52	   that says how to align (usually "re-copy the stub"). A consumer's own next session then
53	   raises a blocking finding and performs the migration in that repo — no per-repo PR from
54	   here.
55	3. Keep the pack's `detect` fingerprint **tolerant of the legacy shape** while copies migrate
56	   (e.g. a `LEGACY_*` list beside the current constant), so a fresh `--init` still recognizes a
57	   not-yet-migrated repo and seeds the pack.
58	
59	Fleet-wide "everyone has migrated" telemetry exists — declare the rename as a
60	[baseline migration](engine/migrations/README.md), **in the same change that introduces the tolerance**: a
61	tolerance that lands without its record has no signal that will ever retire it. Any legacy shape a
62	tolerance keeps readable (an old path, a stub's old form, a legacy key *inside* a consumer's config
63	file) is trackable the same way, `legacyPresent` reading whatever expresses the old shape. The
64	fleet census probes every repo for the legacy shape and **auto-retires** the migration once none
65	remain. While a migration's tolerance still lives inline (readers not yet consulting its
66	`resolvePath`), keep it `retire:'manual'` and drop it deliberately.
67	
68	## Relocating wiring that consumers reference by path
69	
70	What we learned moving the sync hook between homes (#211/#213), and again retiring it (#385):
71	the file is only half the change — every *reference* to its old path is itself a consumer-held
72	copy that won't move on its own, and each needs a channel.
73	
74	- **Enumerate the reference holders before touching the file** — `settings.json` hook commands,
75	  other canon scripts, the fleet routine's discovery probe, docs — then grep for the old path
76	  afterward (the text-sweep skill owns the mechanics). Include state that lives
77	  **outside the repo entirely**: a web environment's pasted Setup script is snapshotted at
78	  environment build, where no check or update run can ever reach it.
79	- **Never break the channel the migration itself travels through.** Fleet discovery finds
80	  members by the tracked `.claudinite-checks.json`; a probe that recognizes only a new shape
81	  doesn't make noise like a wrong check — it **silently and permanently orphans** every
82	  unmigrated repo, since discovery is what reaches them to migrate them. Same for the settings
83	  registration: a session already running when the canon change lands still runs the old wiring,
84	  so the old entry point must keep working until the member's refresh lands (that's what the
85	  stable `engine/hooks/*-command` addresses are for — relocate what they call, not the
86	  addresses).
87	- **References nothing can reach get tolerance in the artifact instead** — prefer a probe that
88	  *detects* staleness (and asks for the one human action) over hoping the stale copy keeps
89	  working.
90	
91	## A vendored file executes in the consumer's context
92	
93	Canon files that ship into consumers — the whole vendor set (`engine/` and the declared packs) —
94	run at their *landed* path inside the consumer's repo, not in the canon checkout they were
95	written and tested in. Before changing one, audit every environment assumption against each
96	context it ships to: **git discovers `.git` by walking upward**, so introspection from a vendored
97	copy answers with the *consumer's* repo unless constrained to the expected toplevel (the
98	`--show-toplevel` guard in `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs` — an unconstrained `rev-parse HEAD` nearly
99	stamped a consumer sha as canon provenance, #340); relative paths resolve against the vendored
100	location; network access and credentials present where the file was written may be absent where it
101	lands. The co-located header comment at the usage site carries each specific trap; this entry is
102	the class.
103	
104	## Normalize requirements to canonical form at the door
105	
106	When a requirement arrives expressed in someone's local context — a schedule in a local
107	timezone, a path from one repo's layout, a phrasing tied to one project's vocabulary — we
108	currently translate it to its canonical form **once, on the way in**, and record only the
109	result. A "nightly at 3:30 my time" request lands in the canon as a fixed UTC cron, stated in
110	UTC and nothing else. The reasoning: the person who asked can carry the original framing;
111	consumers shouldn't inherit it, and the canon shouldn't have to re-explain a conversion (or its
112	edge cases, like DST) forever. If the origin matters for revisiting the decision, it belongs in
113	the issue/PR that made the change, not in the shipped artifact.
114	
115	## How to prove a change is consumer-safe
116	
117	Canon CI is not evidence about consumers. The canon's own packs are always already migrated, so a
118	change that breaks every member passes it green — which is exactly what #555 did, on 2026-07-29,
119	while eleven consumer packs stopped validating and (because a pack that fails validation
120	contributes no rules) their checks stopped running with no other symptom.
121	
122	So there is a procedure, in three layers, cheapest first.
123	
124	**1. The fixture rehearsal — automatic, every PR.** `packs-tests/rehearsal/` builds four fixture
125	consumers, one per shape the fleet has, and runs the REAL converge against your working tree:
126	`apply-vendor-set` → `converge-wiring` → `engine/migrations/apply`, then `engine/selftest.mjs` and
127	`check_the_world`. It runs in **two modes**, and the second is the half people forget:
128	
129	| mode | stamp | answers |
130	|---|---|---|
131	| `fresh` | now | does the ordinary nightly path still work? |
132	| `stale` | pinned in the past | **does it work WITH a migration?** — note selection only fires against an old stamp, so a record that is missing, misdated, or not idempotent shows up here and nowhere else |
133	
134	Adding a shape is the cheap way to cover a case the fixtures don't: a new entry in
135	`fixtures.mjs` is a few lines, and it is one of the two things that discharge the
136	`consumer-safe-change` check.
137	
138	**2. The `consumer-safe-change` check — automatic, work scope.** A change touching a contract
139	consumers hold a copy of (the manifest vocabulary, a blocking rule's severity, the scheduler stub)
140	must ship **either** a migration record **or** a rehearsal fixture. They answer different
141	questions — *members are moved across* versus *members are unharmed* — and both are legitimate.
142	A genuinely additive change needs only the fixture; anything that renames or requires something
143	needs the record, because only a record moves a member that is already out there.
144	
145	**3. The live canary — the required final step of any core change.** A fixture only tests what
146	someone remembered to model. `.github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml` converges a real disposable
147	repo against a canon ref and asks whether it still works: manually via `workflow_dispatch`, and
148	automatically on merge to `main`. Post-merge is still worth having — knowing within minutes beats
149	finding out from the fleet two days later, which is how long #585 went unnoticed.
150	
151	Run it by hand before merging anything structural:
152	`gh workflow run canary-rehearsal.yml -f ref=<your-branch>`. The worker's rehearsal mode converges,
153	reports, and **restores** — no commit, no branch, no stamp. That last one matters: stamping a branch
154	head leaves the member `ref-not-on-trunk`, which the #328 anti-rewind guard then refuses to converge
155	over, so a careless rehearsal wedges the repo it was rehearsing on. That is not hypothetical; it
156	happened by hand to all thirteen members at once on 2026-07-30.
157	
158	**What none of this covers.** A change whose damage is invisible to both the self-test and the
159	conformance sweep — a behaviour change inside a task, say — is still on you to reason about. The
160	layers narrow the class; they do not close it.
161

1	import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
2	import { join } from 'node:path';
3	import { finding } from './findings.mjs';
4	import { parseYaml } from './minimal-yaml.mjs';
5	import { stripComments } from './code-scanning.mjs';
6	import { normalizeEdges, barrierFindings, staleFindings } from './reference-scanning.mjs';
7	
8	// The declarative pattern-check engine: a rule whose whole logic is "these
9	// patterns over these files" is DECLARED as data — and data is JSON, not code.
10	// A pack's declarations live in `packs/<pack>/declared-checks.json` (a skill's
11	// in `<pack>/skills/<name>/declared-checks.json`), an array of specs the pack
12	// registry discovers structurally and compiles here into ordinary
13	// `{ id, severity, why, run(ctx) }` rule objects the runner treats like any
14	// other. Nothing wires them: dropping a declaration into the file adds it.
15	//
16	// The format admits no comments — the pattern plus its failureMessage/what/fix
17	// text IS the check — and no prose pointers: a declaration states its own case
18	// or it isn't finished. So a spec carries exactly:
19	//   id              the rule id settings and findings name it by
20	//   severity        'blocking' | 'advisory'
21	//   failureMessage  why this matters, printed on every finding the rule makes
22	//   …the assertions below, each with the `what` and `fix` it fails with
23	//
24	// REGEXES ARE STRINGS in `/body/flags` form — "/^\\s*schedule:/m" — compiled at
25	// load. Keys that accept a path instead (scanFiles, excludeFiles, pathExists)
26	// read any other string as an exact repo path; at every other pattern key a
27	// string that is not in `/…/` form is an authoring error, reported as one.
28	// The engine owns only the walking (the mechanism/policy line line-scanning.mjs
29	// draws): every pattern, file filter, and failure text stays in the declaration.
30	// Spec keys are deliberately wordy — a declaration must read as the whole check
31	// without this header.
32	//
33	// Built for MANY such rules at once: however many pattern rules a run holds,
34	// the engine makes ONE pass over the scanned tree — each file is read once and
35	// its lines split once, with every subscribing rule's assertions evaluated in
36	// that single visit — and the per-context results are cached, so the first
37	// pattern rule the runner reaches pays for the whole family and the rest are
38	// lookups. Regexes must be non-global (`.test` on a /g regex is stateful).
39	//
40	// Every key at every level is validated against the vocabulary at load — an
41	// unknown key is an authoring error (a typo'd key would otherwise assert
42	// nothing, silently), reported with the container's valid keys.
43	//
44	// The spec vocabulary — everything beyond the rule metadata is optional:
45	//   fix                rule-level default: any assertion declaring `what` but
46	//                      no `fix` of its own inherits this one (for rules whose
47	//                      every assertion shares one remedy)
48	//   scanFiles          which files the content assertions read: a RegExp over
49	//                      repo paths, or one exact path (read directly)
50	//   scanFileClasses    named shared file sets widening the scan scope (unioned
51	//                      with a RegExp scanFiles): javascriptFiles, pythonFiles,
52	//                      markdownFiles, workflowFiles, testFiles
53	//   excludeFileClasses named shared file sets removed from scope (the same
54	//                      class names — testFiles is the usual one)
55	//   scanIgnoringComments  true = content assertions (matchLines, checkEachFile,
56	//                      repoWide) read each file with its JS/TS comments blanked
57	//                      (string-aware, line count preserved — code-scanning.mjs
58	//                      stripComments), so a comment merely naming a forbidden
59	//                      token never fires
60	//   scanIgnoringMarkdownFences  true = content assertions read each markdown
61	//                      file with its fenced code blocks blanked (line count
62	//                      preserved — the view checkSections always gets), so an
63	//                      example inside a fence never satisfies or trips a
64	//                      pattern; non-markdown files are untouched
65	//   scanTracked        true = scan every git-tracked file (mode-independent);
66	//                      default is ctx.files (the run's scanned set —
67	//                      tracked+untracked minus vendored, and only the changed
68	//                      files under --changed)
69	//   excludeFiles       RegExp (or exact path) removing files from scope
70	//   relevantWhen       repo-level relevance, all parts must hold:
71	//                        pathExists / pathAbsent          a path present/absent
72	//                        trackedFileMatches               some tracked path matches
73	//                        noTrackedFileMatches             no tracked path matches
74	//                        exactlyOneTrackedFileMatches     exactly one tracked path matches
75	//                        someTrackedFileContains          { pathMatching, text } — some
76	//                                                         tracked path matching the first
77	//                                                         has text matching the second
78	//                        scanningWholeRepo                true = only under a whole-repo
79	//                                                         sweep (mode 'all'), never a
80	//                                                         --changed run
81	//                        repoContains                     some in-scope file's text
82	//                                                         matches — evaluated only
83	//                                                         if findings exist
84	//   whenMissing        { what, fix } — fires when an exact-path scanFiles is absent
85	//   maxLines           { limit, what, fix } — fires past `limit` lines, anchored there
86	//   maxLineLength      { bytes, what, fix } — one finding per file whose lines
87	//                      run past `bytes` (UTF-8 bytes, so wide characters count
88	//                      what they cost), anchored at the first over-long line;
89	//                      {count}/{longest}/{bytes} interpolate
90	//   skipLinesMatching  RegExp — lines it matches are invisible to matchLines
91	//   matchLines         [{ match, andLineMatches, unlessLineMatches,
92	//                         unlessPreviousLineMatches, whenPathMatches,
93	//                         whenFileMatches, unlessFileMatches, what, fix }]
94	//                      flag each line `match` hits — provided `andLineMatches`
95	//                      (if declared) also hits it, `unlessLineMatches` does
96	//                      not, and `unlessPreviousLineMatches` does not hit the
97	//                      line above (the first line has none) — in files whose
98	//                      path matches `whenPathMatches` (absent = every scanned
99	//                      file), where every `whenFileMatches` matches the text
100	//                      and `unlessFileMatches` does not; per line, the first
101	//                      matching assertion wins
102	//   countMatchingLines [{ linesMatching, atLeast, atMost, what, fix }]
103	//                      per file, the number of lines `linesMatching` hits must
104	//                      sit within the declared bounds (at least one bound;
105	//                      atMost: 0 forbids the pattern); too many anchors at the
106	//                      first line past atMost, too few at the file;
107	//                      {count}/{atLeast}/{atMost} interpolate
108	//   checkEachFile      [{ relevantWhen, whenFileMatches, require, forbid, what, fix }]
109	//                      one finding per file: where every `whenFileMatches`
110	//                      matches, `require` must match / `forbid` must not
111	//                      (`whenFileMatches` takes one RegExp or a list)
112	//   repoWide           [{ unlessSomeFileMatches, flagFilesMatching,
113	//                         neverFlagFiles, what, fix }]
114	//                      unless some in-scope file matches `unlessSomeFileMatches`,
115	//                      flag every file (minus `neverFlagFiles`) satisfying a
116	//                      `flagFilesMatching` group — a list of all-must-match
117	//                      RegExp lists — anchored at the first group's first
118	//                      pattern's first matching line
119	//   requirePaths       [{ path, what, fix }] — each path must exist on disk
120	//   requireIndexCoverage [{ eachTrackedPathMatching | eachScannedPathMatching
121	//                         (+ includeVendored: true to widen scanned to
122	//                         ctx.allFiles), indexFile,
123	//                         coveredByText | coveredByGlobLinesMatching,
124	//                         whenIndexFileAbsent, anchorFindingsAt, what, fix }]
125	//                      every path the quantifier's RegExp matches must be
126	//                      covered in `indexFile`: by containing the filled
127	//                      `coveredByText` template, or — full path or basename —
128	//                      by the first-token glob of some non-comment index line
129	//                      `coveredByGlobLinesMatching` matches. The divergent
130	//                      semantics are declared, never defaulted:
131	//                      whenIndexFileAbsent = "assertNothing" | "flagEveryPath",
132	//                      anchorFindingsAt = "indexFile" (deduped, sorted) |
133	//                      "eachUncoveredPath"
134	//
135	// The structured-data assertions read PARSED documents — `.json` via JSON.parse,
136	// `.yaml`/`.yml` via the minimal YAML parser — each file parsed at most once per
137	// scan, shared by every rule; an absent or unparsable document asserts nothing.
138	// A field path is dot-separated (`devDependencies.esbuild`), and a field counts
139	// as present when its value is not undefined:
140	//   checkParsedFiles   [{ file | filesMatching (+ whereFileContains),
141	//                         forEachEntryAtField, whereEntryFieldEquals:
142	//                           { field, equals },
143	//                         whenFieldPresent,
144	//                         requireField, forbidField,
145	//                         forbidValueInArray: { atField, value, ignoreCase },
146	//                         requireEqualFields: { field, inFile, atField,
147	//                           whenFileMissing, whenUnequal },
148	//                         what, fix }]
149	//                      the select-then-assert family: pick documents (one
150	//                      exact `file`, or every tracked file `filesMatching`
151	//                      whose text matches `whereFileContains`), optionally
152	//                      quantify over the named entries of the object at
153	//                      `forEachEntryAtField` (kept where `whereEntryFieldEquals`
154	//                      holds; {entry} interpolates), gate on `whenFieldPresent`,
155	//                      then assert: `requireField` present / `forbidField`
156	//                      absent / the array at `forbidValueInArray.atField` free
157	//                      of the value / the base's `field` equal to `inFile`'s
158	//                      `atField` (an absent `inFile` fires `whenFileMissing` at
159	//                      its path; a mismatch fires `whenUnequal` with
160	//                      {first}/{second})
161	//   checkKeyValueFile  [{ file, keys, whenMissing, whenLineNotKeyValue,
162	//                         whenKeyUnknown, whenKeyMissing }]
163	//                      the dotenv-style file must exist, hold only KEY=value
164	//                      lines and # comments, use only the declared keys, and
165	//                      declare every one; {key}/{keys}/{line} interpolate
166	//
167	// The reference-barrier assertion — a directed folder-access graph enforced by
168	// the reference-scanning engine (helpers/reference-scanning.mjs, which owns the
169	// edge vocabulary's semantics):
170	//   forbidReferences   [{ from | between | siblings, to, scope, allow, except,
171	//                         matchNames, alsoMatchNames, matchUniqueFilenames,
172	//                         reason }]
173	//                      each entry one barrier edge, normalized at load (a
174	//                      malformed edge is an authoring error); the rule's
175	//                      failureMessage is the why (an edge's `reason` overrides
176	//                      it), and a rule-level `fix` replaces the engine's
177	//                      composed crossing remedy
178	//
179	// The markdown-section assertions read each scanned page's `## ` sections —
180	// headings matched case-insensitively with suffix words allowed, fenced code
181	// blocks invisible, a section running to the next `## ` heading or EOF. A
182	// top-level bullet is a column-0 `-`/`*`/`+` line; a bullet BLOCK is the bullet
183	// plus its indented continuation lines; a DATED bullet leads with its
184	// YYYY-MM-DD run date, bold or plain, validated as a real calendar date. Every
185	// assertion except requirePresent asserts nothing when the section is absent
186	// (presence is its own declared finding, never double-reported):
187	//   checkSections      [{ section | sections: [names], … }] with, each optional:
188	//                        requirePresent                   the `## {section}` heading must exist

624	        dedupKey = path;
625	      }
626	      if (covered) continue;
627	      if (a.anchorFindingsAt === 'indexFile') {
628	        if (!atIndex.has(dedupKey)) atIndex.set(dedupKey, vars);
629	      } else {
630	        j.out.push(finding(j.rule, { file: path, what: fill(a.what, vars), fix: fill(a.fix, vars) }));
631	      }
632	    }
633	    for (const [, vars] of [...atIndex].sort(([k1], [k2]) => k1.localeCompare(k2))) {
634	      j.out.push(finding(j.rule, { file: a.indexFile, what: fill(a.what, vars), fix: fill(a.fix, vars) }));
635	    }
636	  }

639	// The structured-data assertions — they read a few named or tracked documents

642	function assertParsedShape(ctx, j, parsed) {
643	  const s = j.spec;
644

646	  // every tracked file matching), optionally quantify over the named entries
647	  // of the object at forEachEntryAtField, then run every declared assertion
648	  // against each selected base object. An absent or unparsable document
649	  // asserts nothing, as everywhere in the parsed family.
650	  for (const a of s.checkParsedFiles ?? []) {
651	    const paths = a.file !== undefined ? [a.file]
652	      : ctx.tracked.filter((f) =>
653	        a.filesMatching.test(f) && (!a.whereFileContains || a.whereFileContains.test(ctx.read(f) ?? '')));

655	      const doc = parsed(path);
656	      if (doc == null) continue;
657	      let bases;
658	      if (a.forEachEntryAtField) {
659	        const entries = fieldAt(doc, a.forEachEntryAtField);
660	        if (!entries || typeof entries !== 'object' || Array.isArray(entries)) continue;
661	        bases = Object.entries(entries).filter(([, entry]) => entry && typeof entry === 'object');
662	        if (a.whereEntryFieldEquals) {
663	          bases = bases.filter(([, entry]) =>
664	            fieldAt(entry, a.whereEntryFieldEquals.field) === a.whereEntryFieldEquals.equals);
665	        }
666	      } else {

668	      }
669	      for (const [entryName, base] of bases) {
670	        if (a.whenFieldPresent && fieldAt(base, a.whenFieldPresent) === undefined) continue;
671	        const vars = { path, ...(entryName === null ? {} : { entry: entryName }) };
672	        const flag = (what, fix, at = path, extraVars = {}) => j.out.push(finding(j.rule, {
673	          file: at, what: fill(what, { ...vars, ...extraVars }), fix: fill(fix, { ...vars, ...extraVars }),
674	        }));
675	        if (a.requireField && fieldAt(base, a.requireField) === undefined) flag(a.what, a.fix);
676	        if (a.forbidField && fieldAt(base, a.forbidField) !== undefined) flag(a.what, a.fix);
677	        if (a.forbidValueInArray) {
678	          const values = fieldAt(base, a.forbidValueInArray.atField);
679	          const norm = (v) => (a.forbidValueInArray.ignoreCase ? String(v).toLowerCase() : String(v));
680	          if (Array.isArray(values) && values.some((v) => norm(v) === norm(a.forbidValueInArray.value))) {
681	            flag(a.what, a.fix);
682	          }
683	        }
684	        if (a.requireEqualFields) {
685	          const eq = a.requireEqualFields;
686	          if (ctx.read(eq.inFile) === null) {
687	            flag(eq.whenFileMissing.what, eq.whenFileMissing.fix, eq.inFile);
688	          } else {
689	            const targetDoc = parsed(eq.inFile);
690	            if (targetDoc != null) {
691	              const pair = { first: fieldAt(base, eq.field), second: fieldAt(targetDoc, eq.atField) };
692	              if (pair.first !== pair.second) flag(eq.whenUnequal.what, eq.whenUnequal.fix, path, pair);

694	          }
695	        }
696	      }
697	    }
698	  }

700	  for (const a of s.checkKeyValueFile ?? []) {
701	    const keysVar = { keys: a.keys.join(', ') };
702	    const text = ctx.read(a.file);
703	    if (text === null) {
704	      j.out.push(finding(j.rule, { file: a.file, what: fill(a.whenMissing.what, keysVar), fix: fill(a.whenMissing.fix, keysVar) }));
705	      continue;
706	    }
707	    const seen = new Set();
708	    text.split('\n').forEach((raw, i) => {
709	      const line = raw.trim();
710	      if (!line || line.startsWith('#')) return;
711	      const eq = line.indexOf('=');
712	      if (eq === -1) {
713	        const vars = { ...keysVar, line };
714	        j.out.push(finding(j.rule, { file: a.file, line: i + 1, what: fill(a.whenLineNotKeyValue.what, vars), fix: fill(a.whenLineNotKeyValue.fix, vars) }));
715	        return;
716	      }
717	      const key = line.slice(0, eq).trim();
718	      if (!a.keys.includes(key)) {
719	        const vars = { ...keysVar, key };
720	        j.out.push(finding(j.rule, { file: a.file, line: i + 1, what: fill(a.whenKeyUnknown.what, vars), fix: fill(a.whenKeyUnknown.fix, vars) }));
721	      }
722	      seen.add(key);
723	    });
724	    for (const key of a.keys) {
725	      if (seen.has(key)) continue;
726	      const vars = { ...keysVar, key };
727	      j.out.push(finding(j.rule, { file: a.file, what: fill(a.whenKeyMissing.what, vars), fix: fill(a.whenKeyMissing.fix, vars) }));
728	    }
729	  }
730	}
731	
732	// A declared check's barrier edges (forbidReferences, normalized at load into
733	// spec.edges): the reference-scanning engine finds the crossings, the rule's
734	// failureMessage is the why (an edge's own `reason` overrides it per finding),
735	// and a rule-level `fix` replaces the engine's composed remedy on every
736	// crossing finding — the structural fail-closed findings (an empty glob
737	// expansion) keep their own texts. Stale reviewed-exception findings are
738	// judged only on a whole-repo sweep, as everywhere the staleness test runs.
739	function assertReferenceEdges(ctx, j) {
740	  const { findings, stale } = barrierFindings(ctx, j.spec.edges, j.rule);
741	  const scanErrors = findings.some((f) => f.resolved === undefined);
742	  j.out.push(...(j.spec.fix === undefined ? findings
743	    : findings.map((f) => (f.resolved === undefined ? f : { ...f, fix: j.spec.fix }))));
744	  if (ctx.mode === 'all' && !scanErrors) j.out.push(...staleFindings(stale, j.rule));
745	}
746	
747	// One file visited once for every subscribing rule: whole-text assertions and
748	// repo-wide bookkeeping first, then a single walk of the lines shared by all
749	// the rules' line assertions. A rule's scanIgnoring* keys pick its VIEW of the
750	// same file — comments blanked, markdown fences blanked, or both — each view
751	// computed at most once per visit; every blanking preserves line count, so all
752	// views' line numbers agree and the markdown-section index stays on the raw
753	// text (whose fences markdownIndex already blanks itself).
754	function visit(ctx, subs, path, text) {
755	  const fenced = FILE_CLASSES.markdownFiles.test(path);
756	  const viewKey = (j) => (j.spec.scanIgnoringComments ? 'c' : '') +
757	    (j.spec.scanIgnoringMarkdownFences && fenced ? 'f' : '');
758	  const textViews = new Map();
759	  const lineViews = new Map();
760	  const textFor = (j) => {
761	    const key = viewKey(j);
762	    if (!textViews.has(key)) {
763	      let t = text;
764	      if (key.includes('c')) t = stripComments(t);
765	      if (key.includes('f')) t = blankMarkdownFences(t);
766	      textViews.set(key, t);
767	    }
768	    return textViews.get(key);
769	  };
770	  const linesFor = (j) => {
771	    const key = viewKey(j);
772	    if (!lineViews.has(key)) lineViews.set(key, textFor(j).split('\n'));
773	    return lineViews.get(key);
774	  };
775	  const RAW = { spec: {} };
776	  const lines = () => linesFor(RAW);
777	  let mdIndex = null;
778	  const md = () => (mdIndex ??= markdownIndex(text));
779	  const lineJobs = [];
780	
781	  for (const j of subs) {
782	    const s = j.spec;
783	    if (s.checkSections) assertSections(ctx, j, path, md);
784	    if (s.maxLines && lines().length > s.maxLines.limit) {
785	      const vars = { lines: lines().length, limit: s.maxLines.limit };
786	      j.out.push(finding(j.rule, {
787	        file: path, line: s.maxLines.limit + 1,
788	        what: fill(s.maxLines.what, vars), fix: fill(s.maxLines.fix, vars),
789	      }));
790	    }
791	    if (s.maxLineLength) {
792	      const a = s.maxLineLength;
793	      const over = linesFor(j)
794	        .map((ln, i) => ({ n: i + 1, bytes: Buffer.byteLength(ln) }))
795	        .filter((l) => l.bytes > a.bytes);
796	      if (over.length) {
797	        const vars = { count: over.length, bytes: a.bytes, longest: Math.max(...over.map((l) => l.bytes)) };
798	        j.out.push(finding(j.rule, {
799	          file: path, line: over[0].n, what: fill(a.what, vars), fix: fill(a.fix, vars),
800	        }));
801	      }
802	    }
803	    for (const a of s.countMatchingLines ?? []) {
804	      const view = linesFor(j);
805	      let count = 0;
806	      let overflowAt = null;
807	      for (let i = 0; i < view.length; i++) {
808	        if (!a.linesMatching.test(view[i])) continue;
809	        count += 1;
810	        if (overflowAt === null && a.atMost !== undefined && count === a.atMost + 1) overflowAt = i + 1;
811	      }
812	      const under = a.atLeast !== undefined && count < a.atLeast;
813	      if (!under && overflowAt === null) continue;
814	      const vars = { count,
815	        ...(a.atLeast !== undefined ? { atLeast: a.atLeast } : {}),
816	        ...(a.atMost !== undefined ? { atMost: a.atMost } : {}) };
817	      j.out.push(finding(j.rule, {
818	        file: path, ...(under ? {} : { line: overflowAt }),
819	        what: fill(a.what, vars), fix: fill(a.fix, vars),
820	      }));
821	    }
822	    for (const a of s.checkEachFile ?? []) {
823	      if (a.relevantWhen && !relevant(ctx, a.relevantWhen)) continue;
824	      if (!arr(a.whenFileMatches).every((re) => re.test(textFor(j)))) continue;
825	      if (a.forbid ? a.forbid.test(textFor(j)) : !a.require.test(textFor(j))) {
826	        j.out.push(finding(j.rule, { file: path, what: a.what, fix: a.fix }));
827	      }
828	    }
829	    for (const st of j.repoStates) {
830	      if (st.a.unlessSomeFileMatches.test(textFor(j))) st.satisfied = true;
831	      if (excluded(path, st.a.neverFlagFiles)) continue;
832	      const group = st.a.flagFilesMatching.find((g) => g.every((re) => re.test(textFor(j))));
833	      if (group) {
834	        const at = linesFor(j).findIndex((ln) => group[0].test(ln));
835	        st.hits.push({ file: path, line: at === -1 ? null : at + 1, what: st.a.what, fix: st.a.fix });
836	      }
837	    }
838	    const eligible = (s.matchLines ?? []).filter((a) =>
839	      (!a.whenPathMatches || a.whenPathMatches.test(path)) &&
840	      arr(a.whenFileMatches).every((re) => re.test(textFor(j))) && !a.unlessFileMatches?.test(textFor(j)));
841	    if (eligible.length) lineJobs.push({ j, eligible, viewLines: linesFor(j) });
842	  }
843	
844	  if (!lineJobs.length) return;
845	  for (let i = 0; i < lines().length; i++) {
846	    for (const { j, eligible, viewLines } of lineJobs) {
847	      const ln = viewLines[i];
848	      if (j.spec.skipLinesMatching?.test(ln)) continue;
849	      for (const a of eligible) {
850	        const m = ln.match(a.match);
851	        if (!m || (a.andLineMatches && !a.andLineMatches.test(ln)) || a.unlessLineMatches?.test(ln)) continue;
852	        if (a.unlessPreviousLineMatches && i > 0 && a.unlessPreviousLineMatches.test(viewLines[i - 1])) continue;
853	        const vars = { match: m[0] };
854	        j.out.push(finding(j.rule, {
855	          file: path, line: i + 1, what: fill(a.what, vars), fix: fill(a.fix, vars),
856	        }));
857	        break;
858	      }
859	    }
860	  }
861	}
862	
863	function results(ctx) {
864	  let res = scans.get(ctx);
865	  if (res) return res;
866	  res = new Map();
867	  scans.set(ctx, res);
868	
869	  const jobs = [];
870	  for (const rule of REGISTRY) {
871	    const out = [];
872	    res.set(rule, out);
873	    if (!relevant(ctx, rule.spec.relevantWhen)) continue;
874	    jobs.push({
875	      rule, spec: rule.spec, out,
876	      repoStates: (rule.spec.repoWide ?? []).map((a) => ({ a, satisfied: false, hits: [] })),
877	    });
878	  }
879	
880	  const parsedDocs = new Map();
881	  const parsed = (path) => {
882	    if (!parsedDocs.has(path)) {
883	      const text = ctx.read(path);
884	      let doc = null;
885	      if (text !== null) {
886	        if (/\.ya?ml$/.test(path)) doc = parseYaml(text);
887	        else { try { doc = JSON.parse(text); } catch { doc = null; } }
888	      }
889	      parsedDocs.set(path, doc);
890	    }
891	    return parsedDocs.get(path);
892	  };
893	
894	  for (const j of jobs) {
895	    assertTreeShape(ctx, j);
896	    assertParsedShape(ctx, j, parsed);
897	    if (j.spec.edges) assertReferenceEdges(ctx, j);
898	    if (typeof j.spec.scanFiles !== 'string') continue;
899	    const text = ctx.read(j.spec.scanFiles);
900	    if (text === null) {
901	      if (j.spec.whenMissing) {
902	        j.out.push(finding(j.rule, { file: j.spec.scanFiles, what: j.spec.whenMissing.what, fix: j.spec.whenMissing.fix }));
903	      }
904	      continue;
905	    }
906	    visit(ctx, [j], j.spec.scanFiles, text);
907	  }
908	
909	  const swept = jobs.filter((j) => j.spec.scanMatchers.length);
910	  if (swept.length) {
911	    const scanned = new Set(ctx.files);
912	    const tracked = new Set(ctx.tracked);
913	    for (const path of [...ctx.files, ...ctx.tracked.filter((f) => !scanned.has(f))]) {
914	      const subs = swept.filter((j) =>
915	        (j.spec.scanTracked ? tracked : scanned).has(path) &&
916	        j.spec.scanMatchers.some((re) => re.test(path)) && !excluded(path, j.spec.excludeMatchers));
917	      if (!subs.length) continue;
918	      const text = ctx.read(path);
919	      if (text !== null) visit(ctx, subs, path, text);
920	    }
921	  }
922	
923	  for (const j of jobs) {
924	    for (const st of j.repoStates) {
925	      if (!st.satisfied) for (const h of st.hits) j.out.push(finding(j.rule, h));
926	    }
927	    const marker = j.spec.relevantWhen?.repoContains;
928	    if (marker && j.out.length &&
929	        !ctx.files.some((f) => !excluded(f, j.spec.excludeMatchers) && marker.test(ctx.read(f) ?? ''))) {
930	      j.out.length = 0;
931	    }
932	  }
933	  return res;
934	}
935	
936	// Where a declaration says RegExp: keys reading `/body/flags` strings. The two
937	// sets differ in what a NON-regex string means — a path at PATH_OR_PATTERN_KEYS
938	// (scanFiles: "README.md" is read directly), an authoring error anywhere else.
939	const PATH_OR_PATTERN_KEYS = new Set(['scanFiles', 'excludeFiles']);
940	const PATTERN_KEYS = new Set([
941	  'skipLinesMatching', 'match', 'andLineMatches', 'unlessLineMatches',
942	  'unlessPreviousLineMatches', 'whenPathMatches', 'whenFileMatches', 'unlessFileMatches',
943	  'require', 'forbid', 'trackedFileMatches', 'noTrackedFileMatches', 'exactlyOneTrackedFileMatches',
944	  'pathMatching', 'text', 'repoContains', 'unlessSomeFileMatches', 'flagFilesMatching',
945	  'neverFlagFiles', 'eachTrackedPathMatching', 'eachPathMatching', 'globLineMatching',
946	  'filesMatching', 'whereFileContains', 'inFilesMatching', 'pattern', 'linesMatching',
947	  'eachScannedPathMatching', 'coveredByGlobLinesMatching',
948	]);
949	const RE_FORM = /^\/(.*)\/([dgimsuvy]*)$/s;
950	
951	// Compile a spec's pattern strings in place of their keys, leaving every other
952	// value (paths, field names, failure text, numbers) exactly as declared. A real
953	// RegExp passes through, so a spec built in code — the engine's own tests — is
954	// the same object either way.
955	function compileSpec(value, key, where) {
956	  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map((v) => compileSpec(v, key, where));
957	  if (value === null || value instanceof RegExp) return value;
958	  if (typeof value === 'string') {
959	    if (!PATTERN_KEYS.has(key) && !PATH_OR_PATTERN_KEYS.has(key)) return value;
960	    const form = RE_FORM.exec(value);
961	    if (!form) {
962	      if (PATH_OR_PATTERN_KEYS.has(key)) return value;
963	      throw new Error(`${where}: "${key}" takes a regex in /pattern/flags form, not ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
964	    }
965	    try { return new RegExp(form[1], form[2]); }
966	    catch (e) { throw new Error(`${where}: "${key}" is not a valid regex — ${e.message}`); }
967	  }
968	  if (typeof value !== 'object') return value;
969	  const out = {};
970	  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(value)) out[k] = compileSpec(v, k, where);
971	  return out;
972	}
973	
974	export function patternRule(declaration, { selfExclude = null } = {}) {
975	  const where = `the declared check "${declaration.id}"`;
976	  if (typeof declaration.id !== 'string' || !declaration.id.trim()) {
977	    throw new Error('a declared check needs a non-empty "id"');
978	  }
979	  if (declaration.severity !== 'blocking' && declaration.severity !== 'advisory') {
980	    throw new Error(`${where}: severity must be "blocking" or "advisory", not ${JSON.stringify(declaration.severity)}`);
981	  }
982	  validateSpecKeys(declaration, 'spec', where);
983	  const spec = compileSpec(declaration, null, where);
984	  normalizeLegacySpellings(spec);
985	  validateEntryShapes(spec, where);
986	  const classPatterns = (names) => (names ?? []).map((n) => {
987	    if (!FILE_CLASSES[n]) {
988	      throw new Error(`${where}: "${n}" is not a file class — the classes are: ${Object.keys(FILE_CLASSES).join(', ')}`);
989	    }
990	    return FILE_CLASSES[n];
991	  });
992	  const scanClasses = classPatterns(spec.scanFileClasses);
993	  if (scanClasses.length && typeof spec.scanFiles === 'string') {
994	    throw new Error(`${where}: scanFileClasses cannot combine with an exact-path scanFiles`);
995	  }
996	  // The normalized selection surface the scan reads: the sweep patterns
997	  // (regex scanFiles + classes) and every exclusion (declared, class-named,
998	  // and the loader-supplied self-exclusion) as flat lists.
999	  spec.scanMatchers = [...(spec.scanFiles instanceof RegExp ? [spec.scanFiles] : []), ...scanClasses];
1000	  spec.excludeMatchers = [
1001	    ...(spec.excludeFiles != null ? [spec.excludeFiles] : []),
1002	    ...classPatterns(spec.excludeFileClasses),
1003	    ...(selfExclude ? [selfExclude] : []),
1004	  ];
1005	  if (typeof spec.fix === 'string') applyFixDefault(spec, spec.fix);
1006	  if (spec.forbidReferences !== undefined) {
1007	    const { edges, errors } = normalizeEdges(spec.forbidReferences);
1008	    if (errors.length) throw new Error(`${where}: ${errors[0].what} — ${errors[0].fix}`);
1009	    spec.edges = edges;
1010	  }
1011	  const rule = {
1012	    id: spec.id,
1013	    severity: spec.severity,
1014	    why: spec.failureMessage,
1015	    spec,
1016	    run(ctx) { return results(ctx).get(rule); },
1017	  };
1018	  REGISTRY.push(rule);
1019	  return rule;
1020	}
1021	
1022	// A directory's declared checks: `<dir>/declared-checks.json`, an array of specs
1023	// compiled into rules — none when the file is absent. Cached by path, so the
1024	// registry and a test asking the same directory share one set of rule objects
1025	// (two would each re-run the shared scan for the same assertions).
1026	//
1027	// A SKILL's declarations (a dir named `…/skills/<name>`) are compiled with a
1028	// structural self-exclusion — content under any `skills/<name>/` path segment
1029	// pair is out of every assertion's scope — so a skill's own SKILL.md examples
1030	// never trip its checks, in whichever tree the skill's content appears (the
1031	// canon's packs/<pack>/skills/, a root skills/ layout, a consumer's mounted
1032	// .claude/skills/ links), without each declaration hand-spelling the exclusion.
1033	const loaded = new Map();
1034	export function loadDeclaredChecks(dir) {
1035	  const path = join(dir, 'declared-checks.json');
1036	  if (!loaded.has(path)) {
1037	    let specs = [];
1038	    if (existsSync(path)) {
1039	      let raw;
1040	      try { raw = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')); }
1041	      catch (e) { throw new Error(`${path} is not valid JSON: ${e.message}`); }
1042	      if (!Array.isArray(raw)) throw new Error(`${path} must be an array of check declarations`);
1043	      specs = raw;
1044	    }
1045	    const skillName = /(^|[\\/])skills[\\/]([^\\/]+)$/.exec(dir)?.[2];
1046	    const selfExclude = skillName ? new RegExp(`(^|/)skills/${escapeRe(skillName)}/`) : null;
1047	    loaded.set(path, specs.map((s) => patternRule(s, { selfExclude })));
1048	  }
1049	  return loaded.get(path);
1050	}
